a390.speaker: Mohamud Mohamed Hassan, Director of Save the Children in Somalia (statement)
a390.name: Mohamud Mohamed Hassan
a390.title: Director of Save the Children in Somalia (statement)
a390.speech: "We are concerned that the conflict in the Hiran region has interrupted life-saving services for children, including children who were being treated for malnutrition and who were forced to flee health centres with their families." ; Said the organisation's assessment revealed that displaced families are facing severe humanitarian conditions, with many arriving without food, shelter or basic supplies ; "To date, no significant humanitarian aid has been delivered, which underlines the urgent need for a coordinated and unrestricted humanitarian response to meet vital needs."

a390.speaker: Save the Children (NGO)
a390.name: Save the Children (NGO)
a390.speech: Reported that clashes between local militias, government forces and non-state armed groups in Hiran intensified over the past two months, with a significant escalation on 27 July that displaced more than 22,800 people in the town of Mahas alone; that the displaced are sheltering in nearby villages with host families in overcrowded conditions or in the open without access to essential services; that it has had to suspend its activities at 21 health centres because of the conflict, including a stabilisation centre for children with severe acute malnutrition ; Warned that the conflict damaged water sources, blocked access routes and worsened food insecurity, and that women, children and other vulnerable groups lack adequate shelter and suffer strong psychological stress; expressed its "deep concern" at increasing reports of the recruitment of minors by armed actors on both sides; recalled that the new displacement adds to an earlier crisis in communities already hit by severe drought, which caused a significant rise in child malnutrition, aggravated by cuts in humanitarian aid, and that earlier this year 32 health centres it supported in Hiran were closed due to lack of funding.

a390.speaker: Humanitarian partners and local authorities
a390.name: Humanitarian partners and local authorities
a390.speech: According to them, the conflict has displaced about 100,000 people in the Hiran and Gedo (south) regions over the past two months, increasing pressure on already limited resources such as shelter, food, drinking water and health care.

a409.speaker: Michael Wimberly, professor of geography and environmental sustainability at the University of Oklahoma
a409.name: Michael Wimberly
a409.title: professor of geography and environmental sustainability at the University of Oklahoma
a409.speech: “This area has historically been important forest habitat for biodiversity, but elephant populations have declined precipitously because of human encroachment and habitat degradation.”

a409.speaker: Michael Wimberly, professor of geography and environmental sustainability at the University of Oklahoma
a409.name: Michael Wimberly
a409.title: professor of geography and environmental sustainability at the University of Oklahoma
a409.speech: Noted that the drivers of change here are multifaceted: in 2016, drought associated with El Niño parched forests and promoted fires across more than 12 percent of Ghana's moist semi-deciduous and upland evergreen forests.

a409.speaker: Landsat study by Wimberly and a team of researchers in the United States and Ghana (2003–2019)
a409.name: Landsat study by Wimberly and a team of researchers in the United States and Ghana (2003–2019)
a409.speech: Found that although vegetation change was relatively slow from 2003 to 2015, it picked up significantly between 2015 and 2019; overall, there was more forest loss and degradation than recovery, resulting in a gradual decline of tree cover.

a409.speaker: 2024 United Nations report on the state of the world's forests
a409.name: 2024 United Nations report on the state of the world's forests
a409.speech: Highlighted the Forest Data Partnership, an effort to help people in Ghana access remote sensing data to track commodities linked to deforestation and prevent forest loss.

a409.speaker: Satellite images (Landsat 4 and Landsat 9, US Geological Survey data)
a409.name: Satellite images (Landsat 4 and Landsat 9
a409.title: US Geological Survey data)
a409.speech: Indicate that these protected forest remnants have become even smaller in recent decades.

a620.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a620.name: Donald Trump
a620.title: President of the United States
a620.speech: Justifying the withdrawal from the WHO, cited what he called the inappropriate political influence of member states on the global body that is about 20 per cent funded by the US ; "Oooh, that's a big one," he said as he signed the document ; criticised the Geneva-based institution for how it handled COVID-19.

a620.speaker: US executive order withdrawing from the World Health Organisation
a620.name: US executive order withdrawing from the World Health Organisation
a620.speech: "The organisation's mishandling of the COVID-19 pandemic that arose out of Wuhan, China, and other global health crises, its failure to adopt urgently needed reforms, and its inability to demonstrate independence from the inappropriate political influence of WHO member states is the reason for US withdrawal."

a620.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a620.name: Donald Trump
a620.title: President of the United States
a620.speech: According to him, the Paris accord is among several international agreements that do not reflect US values; the agreement only "steers American taxpayer dollars to countries that do not require, or merit, financial assistance in the interests of the American people" ; said that instead of joining a global agreement, "the United States' successful track record of advancing both economic and environmental objectives should be a model for other countries."

a620.speaker: Biden administration
a620.name: Biden administration
a620.speech: According to the Biden administration, the policy, known as CHNV, was initiated and designed to lower illegal border crossings.

a620.speaker: US executive order on foreign assistance
a620.name: US executive order on foreign assistance
a620.speech: "Foreign aid industry and bureaucracy are not aligned with American interests and in many cases antithetical to American values. It serves to destabilise world peace by promoting ideas in foreign countries that are directly inverse to harmonious and stable relations internal to and among countries." ; "No further United States foreign assistance shall be disbursed in a manner that is not fully aligned with the foreign policy of the President of the United States."

a620.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a620.name: Donald Trump
a620.title: President of the United States
a620.speech: Signed an executive order declaring that the US will only recognise the male and female genders, which he said are not changeable and are grounded "in fundamental and incontrovertible reality" ; had earlier noted during his inaugural speech that his administration would recognise only the male and female genders: "As of today, it will henceforth be the official policy of the United States government that there are only two genders, male and female."

a722.speaker: Nigerian government
a722.name: Nigerian government
a722.speech: Announced plans to commence domestic production of HIV commodities, including test kits and anti-retroviral drugs, before the end of 2025.

a722.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General, National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a722.name: Temitope Ilori
a722.title: Director-General, National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a722.speech: Disclosed this on Friday in Ilorin during the inauguration of the Kwara Prevention of Mother to Child Transmission (PMTCT) and Paediatrics ART Acceleration Committee ; explained that the initiative was part of the government’s broader efforts to eliminate AIDS as a public health threat by 2030, with other measures including enrolling individuals in the National Health Insurance Scheme, mobilising resources for states, enhancing advocacy campaigns, and supporting research into HIV vaccines ; noted that establishing the committee was aimed at achieving an AIDS-free generation and ensuring a sustainable HIV response.

a722.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General, National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a722.name: Temitope Ilori
a722.title: Director-General, National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a722.speech: “UNAIDS 2023 reports indicate that approximately 140,000 children aged 0-14 are living with HIV, with 22,000 new infections and 15,000 AIDS-related deaths occurring annually. Despite progress, PMTCT and paediatric HIV coverage remains below 33 per cent far from the 95 per cent target” ; “To address this, the Global Alliance Action Plan to End AIDS in Children was developed in 2021 with full financial support, yet coverage remains suboptimal” ; highlighted that although Kwara’s HIV prevalence rate of 0.8 per cent is below the national average of 1.4 per cent, significant disparities remain; said women are disproportionately affected, with a prevalence of 1.3 per cent compared to 0.4 per cent in men; added that some local governments still require targeted interventions to reduce prevalence further ; “Achieving an AIDS-free generation is within reach and no child should be born HIV-positive in Kwara State” ; urges all partners to support the government in developing a comprehensive line-list of children of HIV-positive clients which is crucial to accelerating paediatric ART nationwide.

a722.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General, National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a722.name: Temitope Ilori
a722.title: Director-General, National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a722.speech: Noted that the Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Iziaq Salako, had established a National Acceleration Committee, and the model is being replicated at the state level to eliminate mother-to-child transmission and enhance real-time monitoring of HIV programmes.

a722.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General, National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a722.name: Temitope Ilori
a722.title: Director-General, National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a722.speech: Highlighted the need for government-led sustainability efforts to address government’s continued reliance on donor support: “Over the past few days, I have received numerous calls regarding the implications of the 90-day foreign aid suspension on our HIV programme. While we are relieved that HIV services remain exempt, this situation underscores the need for government-led sustainability efforts” ; said government approaches include integrating HIV services into the national health system and strengthening government-mandated structures; added that other measures included partners providing technical assistance as well as ensuring timely release of state and local government funds for HIV programmes; said government was also developing sustainable non-health components of the response and empowering civil society to serve as advocates and community service providers.

a722.speaker: Kayode Alabi, Deputy Governor of Kwara State and Chairman of Kwara State AIDS Control Agency
a722.name: Kayode Alabi
a722.title: Deputy Governor of Kwara State and Chairman of Kwara State AIDS Control Agency
a722.speech: Gave an assurance that the state government would ensure the committee achieved its mandate, and said MTCT of HIV would be a thing of the past with the committee in place.

a722.speaker: UNAIDS 2023 reports
a722.name: UNAIDS 2023 reports
a722.speech: Indicate that approximately 140,000 children aged 0-14 are living with HIV, with 22,000 new infections and 15,000 AIDS-related deaths occurring annually.

a1224.speaker: International AIDS Society (IAS) (statement signed by Beatriz Grinsztejn, IAS President)
a1224.name: International AIDS Society (IAS) (statement signed by Beatriz Grinsztejn
a1224.title: IAS President)
a1224.speech: Has warned that the immediate freezing of funding to the U.S. President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), including a stop-work order for existing grants and contracts, portends a looming crisis for millions worldwide, and places millions of lives in jeopardy.

a1224.speaker: Beatriz Grinsztejn, IAS President
a1224.name: Beatriz Grinsztejn
a1224.title: IAS President
a1224.speech: "This is a matter of life or death." ; "PEPFAR provides lifesaving antiretrovirals for more than 20 million people – and stopping its funding essentially stops their HIV treatment. If that happens, people are going to die and HIV will resurge." ; "It makes no sense to suddenly stop this incredible catalyst of our global progress towards ending HIV as a threat to public health and individual well-being."

a1224.speaker: PEPFAR (official statement)
a1224.name: PEPFAR (official statement)
a1224.speech: "PEPFAR's lifesaving work is enabled through the U.S. government's unwavering commitment to the program and the American people's compassion and generosity, as PEPFAR ensures every U.S. taxpayer dollar is optimally focused for impact."

a1224.speaker: International AIDS Society (IAS)
a1224.name: International AIDS Society (IAS)
a1224.speech: Urgently calls on policy makers and stakeholders to restore the funding lifeline to this pivotal programme. Lives depend on it, right now.

a1239.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a1239.name: Donald Trump
a1239.title: U.S. President
a1239.speech: announced on Monday the suspension of military assistance to Ukraine as he seeks to pressure Volodymyr Zelenskyy to engage in peace talks with Russia; told reporters earlier on Monday that he does not rule out a pause.

a1239.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President, and JD Vance, Vice President
a1239.name: Donald Trump
a1239.title: U.S. President, and JD Vance, Vice President
a1239.speech: reproached Zelenskyy in a tense Oval Office meeting for not being allegedly grateful enough for Washington’s military aid and hesitant on a diplomatic approach to end the war with Russia.

a1239.speaker: White House official (anonymous)
a1239.name: White House official (anonymous)
a1239.speech: told French news agency AFP on condition of anonymity that Trump is focused on reaching a peace deal and the military aid pause will remain in place until Zelenskyy has made a commitment to seeking peace talks: “We are pausing and reviewing our aid to ensure that it is contributing to a solution. The President has been clear that he is focused on peace. We need our partners to be committed to that goal as well.”

a1239.speaker: CNN sources
a1239.name: CNN sources
a1239.speech: according to them, the disruption in the flow of US arms to the front line would rapidly weaken Ukraine’s chance of pushing back invading Russian troops.

a1239.speaker: Gregory Meeks, top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee
a1239.name: Gregory Meeks
a1239.title: top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee
a1239.speech: said “My Republican colleagues who have called Putin a war criminal and promised their continued support to Ukraine must join me in demanding President Trump immediately lift this disastrous and unlawful freeze.”

a1239.speaker: The New York Times
a1239.name: The New York Times
a1239.speech: reported that the pause has gone into effect immediately and impacts hundreds of millions of dollars of weaponry in the process of being sent to Ukraine.

a1239.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a1239.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a1239.title: President of Ukraine
a1239.speech: said Monday he was seeking for the war to end “as soon as possible”; accused Russia of not being serious about peace; insisted tough security guarantees were the only way to end the war.

a1580.speaker: Communiqué of the Council of Ministers of 12 August 2024 (Niger)
a1580.name: Communiqué of the Council of Ministers of 12 August 2024 (Niger)
a1580.speech: Was clear and utterly peremptory: the government's decision to take charge, from its own funds, of flood prevention and management operations means that all related activities and actions will fall to the State, to the State alone, in line with the affirmation of national sovereignty. The State of Niger decided to allocate, from its own funds, an envelope of 12 billion CFA francs for flood prevention and management operations.

a1580.speaker: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland (CNSP), Head of State of Niger
a1580.name: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani
a1580.title: President of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland (CNSP), Head of State of Niger
a1580.speech: Gave instructions for an amount of 2 billion CFA francs from the recoveries of the Commission for the Fight against Financial and Fiscal Crime (CoLDEFF) to be immediately allocated to the flood prevention and management operations.

a1580.speaker: Nigerien Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation (communiqué)
a1580.name: Nigerien Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation (communiqué)
a1580.speech: Through its communiqué it was learned that the EU had made available to Niger, without the country having requested it, support of 1.3 million euros, seemingly to assist the victims of the floods that occurred in the country.

a1580.speaker: European Union
a1580.name: European Union
a1580.speech: After the discovery of the affair by the CNSP and the government, the EU broke into a lament through a great deal of literature which, moreover, confirms the facts revealed by the Nigerien authorities.

a1580.speaker: Nigerien authorities
a1580.name: Nigerien authorities
a1580.speech: Faced with this disrespectful act which flouts the dignity of the sons and daughters of the Nation, disregards all rules of propriety and violates diplomatic usages, the authorities requested the recall of the EU Ambassador, Mr. Salvador Pinto Da Franca; the decision to recall the ambassador indeed originates from Niger.

a1580.speaker: State of Niger
a1580.name: State of Niger
a1580.speech: Has decided to commission an audit of the management of the EU's so-called funds to discover the winding circuits and parallel channels they have irrigated.

a1581.speaker: Dr. Samuel Toe, Deputy Education Minister for Planning, Research, and Development, Liberia
a1581.name: Dr. Samuel Toe
a1581.title: Deputy Education Minister for Planning, Research, and Development, Liberia
a1581.speech: Disclosed at the Ministry of Information's regular press briefing that the Government of Liberia, through the Ministry of Education, is due to launch a National School Census data collection, and indicated that a gap in data collection has been noted since the last national school census in 2020, which this new initiative aims to fill and provide updated information on the state of education in the country. He emphasized that they take their mandate under the 2011 Education Reform Act and the Education Sector Plans seriously.

a1581.speaker: Dr. Samuel Toe, Deputy Education Minister for Planning, Research, and Development, Liberia
a1581.name: Dr. Samuel Toe
a1581.title: Deputy Education Minister for Planning, Research, and Development, Liberia
a1581.speech: "Under this year's census collection, a comprehensive set of data from formal and non-formal TVET institutions across the entire sector will be gathered." ; "This will enable the Ministry to plan more effectively, prepare for proper investments in the education sector, and monitor the quality, access, and equity of the education system in the country."

a1581.speaker: Dr. Samuel Toe, Deputy Education Minister for Planning, Research, and Development, Liberia
a1581.name: Dr. Samuel Toe
a1581.title: Deputy Education Minister for Planning, Research, and Development, Liberia
a1581.speech: Revealed that the ministry has projected a cost of $1.2 million, which will cover equipment purchase, training of data staff, logistics, census reporting, and disseminating the census report.

a1581.speaker: Dr. Samuel Toe, Deputy Education Minister for Planning, Research, and Development, Liberia
a1581.name: Dr. Samuel Toe
a1581.title: Deputy Education Minister for Planning, Research, and Development, Liberia
a1581.speech: "This year's data collection will differ from past procedures, where data enumerators were deployed nationwide. In Montserrado, private school principals and registrars will be responsible for collecting school data and reporting it directly to us this year."

a1581.speaker: Dr. Samuel Toe, Deputy Education Minister for Planning, Research, and Development, Liberia
a1581.name: Dr. Samuel Toe
a1581.title: Deputy Education Minister for Planning, Research, and Development, Liberia
a1581.speech: Stated that they have established a working group comprising key government stakeholders, including the legislature, the Ministry of Youth and Sports, and development partners, to focus on education data and census data collection: "The technical working group on data evidence is responsible for preparing and managing the execution of this year's census and has mobilized resources for this purpose." He noted that activities will include training data management staff, procuring equipment, upgrading their department to an education information management system, and ongoing community mobilization and public information dissemination outreach.

a1581.speaker: Dr. Samuel Toe, Deputy Education Minister for Planning, Research, and Development, Liberia
a1581.name: Dr. Samuel Toe
a1581.title: Deputy Education Minister for Planning, Research, and Development, Liberia
a1581.speech: Speaking on behalf of the Ministry of Education's senior management team, stated that under the community engagement process for this year's census collection, they will involve the Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs) from private, public, and faith-based schools across Liberia.

a1581.speaker: Dr. Samuel Toe, Deputy Education Minister for Planning, Research, and Development, Liberia
a1581.name: Dr. Samuel Toe
a1581.title: Deputy Education Minister for Planning, Research, and Development, Liberia
a1581.speech: Indicated that the group began its public awareness and media community engagements on October 28, 2024, which will run until December 15, 2024, and that a school census tool distribution process will roll out on December 15: "The testing of this system will take place from November 13 to 15, 2024, and will be conducted by our trainers." He also revealed that a small group will be established to train data personnel, including school administrators, scheduled for November 18 to 23, 2024, with data collection beginning December 1 and running through December 15.

a1851.speaker: Dr Abdullah Mkiga, TARI's Kifyulilo Research Centre manager and project lead
a1851.name: Dr Abdullah Mkiga
a1851.title: TARI's Kifyulilo Research Centre manager and project lead
a1851.speech: Said the initiative has already trained over 500 stakeholders including 324 farmers and 31 agricultural officers from the Siha and Muheza districts: "Farmers have shown great interest in these technologies, but access to pest control inputs remains a challenge. We've now involved agro-dealers and private companies in the training sessions to link them directly with farmers and ensure a steady supply chain."

a1851.speaker: George Mbaga, Tanga Regional Agriculture Officer
a1851.name: George Mbaga
a1851.title: Tanga Regional Agriculture Officer
a1851.speech: Welcomed the initiative, noting that pest infestations especially from fruit flies have long hindered productivity in the region: "Most councils in Tanga grow mangoes and oranges, except some areas of Lushoto and Bumbuli. The introduction of IPM technologies will boost both productivity and quality, helping farmers to earn more."

a1851.speaker: Dr Shepard Ndlela, researcher with icipe
a1851.name: Dr Shepard Ndlela
a1851.title: researcher with icipe
a1851.speech: Explained that effective pest control could open doors to both domestic and export markets: "Fruit farming is profitable, but quality is key. If farmers adopt these techniques, they won't just protect their harvests they'll also gain access to better markets."

a1851.speaker: Ms Juliana Swai, agro-inputs dealer in Muheza
a1851.name: Ms Juliana Swai
a1851.title: agro-inputs dealer in Muheza
a1851.speech: "These technologies are easy to apply. When used together, they make pest control manageable for small-scale farmers."

a1851.speaker: Mr Ismail Gunga, mango and orange grower from Ngomeni village
a1851.name: Mr Ismail Gunga
a1851.title: mango and orange grower from Ngomeni village
a1851.speech: "I've learned to distinguish between harmful and beneficial insects something I didn't know before."

a1859.speaker: Presidency of the Republic of Cabo Verde (note sent to the media)
a1859.name: Presidency of the Republic of Cabo Verde (note sent to the media)
a1859.speech: Explained that the participation of the Nation's Highest Magistrate in the ceremony, which takes place next Monday, the 6th, in Dallas, Texas, fits within the excellent relations between the two countries: "And it amounts to a distinction for Cabo Verde, in recognition of the exemplary implementation of the two Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) Compacts allocated to the country, which has already been selected for a 3rd Compact, now focused on regional integration."

a1859.speaker: Presidency of the Republic of Cabo Verde (note sent to the media)
a1859.name: Presidency of the Republic of Cabo Verde (note sent to the media)
a1859.speech: Stressed that, with a total value of around 200 million dollars, the two MCA Compacts made possible major investments in the islands, particularly in infrastructure, water supply and sanitation; and considered that the invitation to Cabo Verde is also a recognition of the country for its positive performance in terms of good governance, transparency and accountability in the management of public affairs and investment in people.

a1859.speaker: Presidency of the Republic of Cabo Verde (note sent to the media)
a1859.name: Presidency of the Republic of Cabo Verde (note sent to the media)
a1859.speech: "The visit will also be an opportunity for important bilateral meetings with US authorities."

a1929.speaker: Zambia Daily Mail (report dated 25th February 2025)
a1929.name: Zambia Daily Mail (report dated 25th February 2025)
a1929.speech: As reported by the Zambia Daily Mail dated 25th February 2025, 9 Memorandum of Understanding were signed including in the field of Agriculture.

a1929.speaker: World Bank data
a1929.name: World Bank data
a1929.speech: According to the World Bank data, Egypt reached 100% electrification in 2022 meaning the entire population has access to electricity.

a1929.speaker: Statista.com report, "Distribution of electricity consumption in Egypt by 2022"
a1929.name: Statista.com report
a1929.title: "Distribution of electricity consumption in Egypt by 2022"
a1929.speech: According to the report, households were the largest electricity consumer in Egypt; as of April 2022, electricity consumed by individuals in their homes represented 37.6 percent of the consumed electricity in the country, the industrial sector followed with a share of almost 30.4 percent, and public utilities and governmental agencies were the third largest electricity consuming sector.

a1929.speaker: UN Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7
a1929.name: UN Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7
a1929.speech: calls for universal access to clean, affordable and sustainable energy for all by the year 2030.

a1929.speaker: Electricity Cost of Service Study, commissioned by the Energy Regulation Board (ERB)
a1929.name: Electricity Cost of Service Study
a1929.title: commissioned by the Energy Regulation Board (ERB)
a1929.speech: made recommendations following which Zambia adopted a 5-year plan from 2022 to 2027 to abolish the electricity subsidies.

a1929.speaker: Transnational Institute 2023 report, "Egypt: A tale of Class War and Greenwashing"
a1929.name: Transnational Institute 2023 report
a1929.title: "Egypt: A tale of Class War and Greenwashing"
a1929.speech: According to the report, the IMF has been pivotal in shaping economic policy in Egypt over recent years with Egypt currently the largest borrower from the IMF second only to Argentina.

a1929.speaker: Industry reports
a1929.name: Industry reports
a1929.speech: According to Industry reports Egypt generates at least 80% of electricity from one source of energy — fossil fuel — with the rest coming from hydro and renewable energy while Zambia's generation mix is at least 80% hydro.

a1929.speaker: International Energy Agency (IEA)
a1929.name: International Energy Agency (IEA)
a1929.speech: As correctly reported by the International Energy Agency (IEA), Egypt has initiated a number of energy sector reforms, gradually reducing electricity subsidies and introducing feed-in tariffs to promote renewable energy production.

a2017.speaker: Dr. Omary Ubuguyu, Assistant Director for Non-Communicable Diseases at the Ministry of Health (Tanzania)
a2017.name: Dr. Omary Ubuguyu
a2017.title: Assistant Director for Non-Communicable Diseases at the Ministry of Health (Tanzania)
a2017.speech: Revealed that the Tanzanian government, through the Ministry of Health, has continued to strengthen reproductive health services across the country to minimize the negative effects of unsafe childbirth, including the rise of non-communicable diseases such as epilepsy and child malnutrition ; stated that, according to statistics for the 2024/25 period, a total of 192,000 epilepsy cases were reported in health facilities across the country, and noted that the SHINE project will play a vital role in efforts to reduce the impact of the disease, particularly among children.

a2017.speaker: Valentina Decao, Director of the Italian organization COMSOL
a2017.name: Valentina Decao
a2017.title: Director of the Italian organization COMSOL
a2017.speech: Explained that SHINE has been implemented over two years in the regions of Dar es Salaam, Morogoro, and Mbeya. She emphasised that the project focused on educating communities on the best practices for caring for children with epilepsy, including the importance of proper nutrition and appropriate healthcare.

a2017.speaker: Parents of children with epilepsy who attended the event
a2017.name: Parents of children with epilepsy who attended the event
a2017.speech: Shared testimonies about how the project has positively impacted the health and well-being of their children. They called on society to stop stigmatizing children living with the condition and instead offer them love, support, and understanding.

a2043.speaker: Official budget documents and media reporting (early 2025)
a2043.name: Official budget documents and media reporting (early 2025)
a2043.speech: According to official budget documents and corroborated by media reporting in early 2025, the national budget for BCS has been increased to PHP 79.9 million for the fiscal year 2025.

a2043.speaker: Local media monitoring groups and journalists (reports, March–April 2024)
a2043.name: Local media monitoring groups and journalists (reports
a2043.title: March–April 2024)
a2043.speech: Reports from local media monitoring groups and journalists in March–April 2024 reaffirmed the bureau's role as a communications vehicle rather than an independent journalistic institution.

a2043.speaker: Dragomir, M. (2025), State Media Monitor Global Dataset 2025, Media and Journalism Research Center (MJRC)
a2043.name: Dragomir
a2043.title: M. (2025), State Media Monitor Global Dataset 2025, Media and Journalism Research Center (MJRC)
a2043.speech: Cited as the source of the profile: "This article/profile is part of the State Media Monitor Global Dataset 2025, a continuously updated dataset published by the Media and Journalism Research Center (MJRC)."

a2249.speaker: Ghanaian authorities
a2249.name: Ghanaian authorities
a2249.speech: Say the suspect played a central role in the botched smuggling attempt and will face prosecution per Ghana's narcotics laws.

a2249.speaker: Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) (statement dated August 12, 2025)
a2249.name: Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) (statement dated August 12
a2249.speech: "The Commission appreciates all who assisted and continue to support NACOC in its operations against illicit drug trafficking."

a2249.speaker: Ghanaian authorities
a2249.name: Ghanaian authorities
a2249.speech: Declared two other key suspects, Lincoln Nii OKAIJA (born March 27, 1979) and Kate DAVIDSON, alias "Esi", as wanted persons, urging the public to provide any information that could lead to their capture.

a2249.speaker: NACOC 2022 statistics
a2249.name: NACOC 2022 statistics
a2249.speech: According to NACOC's 2022 statistics, the commission seized a record-breaking 59,900 kg of illicit drugs that year, a significant increase from 15,458 kg in 2021.

a2249.speaker: NACOC officials
a2249.name: NACOC officials
a2249.speech: Have reaffirmed their unwavering commitment to dismantling drug networks across the country ; have appealed to residents to remain vigilant and to report any suspicious drug-related activities in their communities, emphasising that public cooperation is paramount to their success in ensuring a drug-free Ghana.

a2297.speaker: Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO)
a2297.name: Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO)
a2297.speech: has issued a number of recommendations to Benin and to the UEMOA countries for better performance: strengthen the promotion and production of import-substitution goods and services within UEMOA and, more specifically for Benin, continue the efforts to diversify the economy. At the regional level, UEMOA member countries should continue implementing measures to promote the production of import-substitution goods and services, which weigh on external trade.

a2297.speaker: Report on Benin's balance of payments for the year 2020 (BCEAO)
a2297.name: Report on Benin's balance of payments for the year 2020 (BCEAO)
a2297.speech: "These measures could notably address the lifting of the constraints that hamper the dynamism and competitiveness of the Union's private sector, notably through policies favouring a reduction in factor costs and support for exports; the deepening of structural reforms, through the consolidation of common sectoral policies in the areas of transport and tourism as well as the continued restructuring of the agricultural value chains; the strengthening of infrastructure (transport, energy, telecommunications, finance)." ; Its conclusions indicate that efforts are being made in public finances in Benin, and that at the national level it will be necessary to continue diversifying the economy, strengthen trade relations with Nigeria, keep the business climate attractive and use Public-Private Partnerships, strengthen the energy supply in line with the second compact of the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA), consolidate domestic resource mobilisation and preserve public debt sustainability. ; It shows that the overall balance of payments posted a surplus of 306,937.9 million CFA francs in 2020, following the surplus (45,550.6 million) of 2019, and that the International Investment Position in 2020 shows net financial liabilities of 2,974,227.7 million as at 31 December 2020 against 2,974,804.5 million as at 31 December 2019.

a2452.speaker: More than 209 former European diplomats, including 110 former EU ambassadors and senior officials, 99 former ambassadors from France, Germany and Italy and 25 senior directors-general (open letter to EU institutions)
a2452.name: More than 209 former European diplomats
a2452.title: including 110 former EU ambassadors and senior officials, 99 former ambassadors from France, Germany and Italy and 25 senior directors-general (open letter to EU institutions)
a2452.speech: Demanded urgent and concrete measures to press Israel to end the war in the Gaza Strip and to respect international law; expressed concern about the Israeli government's plans to evacuate one million Palestinians from Gaza City and its suburbs by forcing them to relocate to concentrated areas in the south in preparation for possible mass deportations to third countries, which carries the risk of a migration crisis.

a2452.speaker: More than 209 former European diplomats (open letter)
a2452.name: More than 209 former European diplomats (open letter)
a2452.speech: Added: “It is estimated that since the letter of 28 July alone, more than 2,600 Palestinians in Gaza have been killed, most of them women and children, and more than 12,000 people have been injured.”

a2452.speaker: More than 209 former European diplomats (open letter)
a2452.name: More than 209 former European diplomats (open letter)
a2452.speech: Pointed out that inadequate humanitarian access to the Gaza Strip has been aggravated by the Israeli government preventing UNRWA and international NGOs from delivering aid since 2 March, that the militarisation of aid deliveries violates all UN humanitarian principles and has led to the death or wounding of thousands of desperate and hungry Palestinians, and that international journalists are denied access to Gaza while over 200 local journalists and media workers have been killed, including eleven in the most recent targeted attacks.

a2452.speaker: More than 209 former European diplomats (open letter)
a2452.name: More than 209 former European diplomats (open letter)
a2452.speech: Addressed the Israeli ministers' approval of plans to build 3,400 housing units in the Palestinian area E1, separating East Jerusalem from the West Bank, stressing that the explicitly stated objective is to sabotage the two-state solution supported by the great majority of UN and EU member states, the only viable possibility for the two peoples to live in peace and security ; “Violent settlers are continuing their actions in the West Bank, which have led, among other things, to the killing of Odeh Hadhalin, a well-known peaceful human rights activist in the West Bank.”

a2452.speaker: More than 209 former European diplomats (open letter)
a2452.name: More than 209 former European diplomats (open letter)
a2452.speech: Expressed deep disappointment that the EU is not responding substantially to the deteriorating situation in Gaza nor pressing Israel to end its brutal war, resume vital humanitarian aid from important donors and end the illegal occupation, stressing that if the EU takes no effective stance only member states would act individually or in “groups of like-minded states” ; “It will not have the full effect of collective action at EU level, and in the annex to this letter the concrete measures are set out which EU member states are called upon to take.”

a2452.speaker: More than 209 former European diplomats (open letter)
a2452.name: More than 209 former European diplomats (open letter)
a2452.speech: Stressed that conditions in Gaza and the West Bank are unprecedented and that their repeated and urgent call to action reflects deep concern about unjustified retaliatory measures and terrible violations of international humanitarian law and human rights committed daily by the Israeli government against the Palestinian people ; “It also reflects our sincere wish that the European Union, to which we have devoted our professional lives, show genuine leadership worthy of the great majority of European citizens who are deeply concerned about the current dire situation in Palestine, and which is in line with European core values and our credibility towards the countries of the Global South. Among other things, inaction undermines efforts to mobilise support for the EU's position on the war in Ukraine.” ; stressed that states and institutions which claim to support human rights and respect international law must lead by example not only with words but through deeds.

a2452.speaker: More than 209 former European diplomats (annex to the open letter)
a2452.name: More than 209 former European diplomats (annex to the open letter)
a2452.speech: Called on EU member states to suspend or revoke arms export licences to Israel including dual-use equipment; end financing of nationally co-financed projects involving Israeli companies and withdraw from Horizon Europe joint research agreements where funding supports acts contrary to international law; instruct public universities to cease cooperation with Israeli bodies suspected of involvement in atrocious crimes; implement national sanctions regimes including visa bans and asset freezes; ban trade in goods and services from illegal settlements; exclude companies linked to illegal settlements from public tenders, state investments and sovereign wealth funds; ban Israeli military ships and aircraft from ports and airspace; prosecute suspected Israeli and Palestinian war criminals under universal jurisdiction and support the ICC; and prevent Europe-based data centres and platforms from processing Israeli government data connected with its activities in the occupied territories.

a2452.speaker: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) report of 22 October
a2452.name: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) report of 22 October
a2452.speech: States that a man-made famine currently prevails in those areas of Gaza, where half a million people are exposed to hunger, misery and death; malnutrition threatens the lives of 132,000 children under five by June 2026, and by the end of September 2025 an estimated 640,000 people (one third of the population) will be affected by catastrophic food insecurity; more than 200 Gazans, including over 60 children, have lost their lives due to malnutrition.

a2481.speaker: Saliem Fakir, founder and executive director of the African Climate Foundation, and Prabhat Upadhyaya, adviser on the G20 and Multilateral Affairs to the African Climate Foundation (commentary)
a2481.name: Saliem Fakir
a2481.title: founder and executive director of the African Climate Foundation, and Prabhat Upadhyaya, adviser on the G20 and Multilateral Affairs to the African Climate Foundation (commentary)
a2481.speech: Write that amid economic fragmentation and political disarray, the Global South and philanthropic organisations should take a pragmatic approach to protecting development gains and pursuing climate resilience, by building issue-based coalitions, strengthening domestic institutions, and making the most of opportunities to lead on the global stage such as South Africa's G20 presidency and India's turn as BRICS+ chair in 2026; argue that efforts to close the climate-finance gap have fallen short and the New Collective Quantified Goal agreed at COP29 in Baku is grossly inadequate, with the situation set to deteriorate as America retreats inward and other developed countries significantly increase defence spending; note that as flows of official development assistance dry up and global debt reaches a record high, developing innovative ways to mobilise domestic and foreign capital has become an urgent priority; and urge that philanthropies expand their reach, improve coordination among themselves, situate climate action in a development context, and collaborate with governments, grassroots organisations and development banks.

a2481.speaker: UN Environment Programme (2024 Emissions Gap Report)
a2481.name: UN Environment Programme (2024 Emissions Gap Report)
a2481.speech: According to the UN Environment Programme, updated Nationally Determined Contributions will need to be more ambitious if the world is to stay within the 1.5C warming threshold; according to its 2024 Emissions Gap Report, there is a need for NDCs that are better aligned with the Paris agreement's pathway for limiting the rise in global temperatures to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.

a2549.speaker: Government of Somaliland
a2549.name: Government of Somaliland
a2549.speech: Has officially declared a humanitarian emergency, warning that millions of people across four regions are facing severe food and water shortages due to prolonged drought conditions.

a2549.speaker: Abdirahman Abdillahi Irro, President of Somaliland
a2549.name: Abdirahman Abdillahi Irro
a2549.title: President of Somaliland
a2549.speech: Made an urgent appeal to international donors and Somalilanders at home and abroad to support relief efforts aimed at saving lives and livelihoods: “Communities in coastal regions such as Salal, Saahil, Sanaag, and Awdal are experiencing extreme hardship” ; “The drought has devastated both people and livestock, threatening the very survival of affected families” ; emphasized that the worsening drought has rendered key grazing areas barren and dried up many water wells, leaving pastoralist communities without vital resources ; “Food shortages, thirst, and displacement have already begun” ; “Women, children, and the elderly are especially vulnerable” ; “We are calling for a unified and compassionate response to save lives” ; “Timely support could prevent a humanitarian catastrophe”.

a2549.speaker: Hussein Adan Igeh Deyr, Somaliland government spokesperson
a2549.name: Hussein Adan Igeh Deyr
a2549.title: Somaliland government spokesperson
a2549.speech: Stated that the committee will focus on mobilizing resources and organizing emergency distributions of food, water, and livestock fodder to affected areas.

a2549.speaker: Sakariye Abdi, local aid worker recently returned from Awdal region
a2549.name: Sakariye Abdi
a2549.title: local aid worker recently returned from Awdal region
a2549.speech: “If the situation persists for several more weeks, we risk large-scale animal deaths, which will have a devastating impact on already fragile households” ; “The consequences could be particularly severe for women, children, and the elderly.”

a2549.speaker: Somaliland cabinet ministers
a2549.name: Somaliland cabinet ministers
a2549.speech: Have pledged to donate one month's salary to the drought relief effort.

a2549.speaker: Kaab TV (reports received)
a2549.name: Kaab TV (reports received)
a2549.speech: Reports received by Kaab TV indicate that Awdal is among the worst-hit regions, with rural communities struggling to find water for both people and animals, and many areas seeing a sharp increase in livestock deaths due to extreme dehydration.

a2549.speaker: United Nations
a2549.name: United Nations
a2549.speech: Has raised alarm over the crisis, estimating that 4.4 million people across Somalia and Somaliland are currently affected by drought-related food and water shortages, and warned that the lack of international funding for its 2025 Humanitarian Appeal — partly due to cuts by the Donald Trump administration — could further limit humanitarian assistance.

a2656.speaker: Koblavi-Dibi Michel, President of the Board of Directors of the Federation of professional agricultural organisations of rubber producers of Côte d’Ivoire (Fph-CI)
a2656.name: Koblavi-Dibi Michel
a2656.title: President of the Board of Directors of the Federation of professional agricultural organisations of rubber producers of Côte d’Ivoire (Fph-CI)
a2656.speech: “By 2040, nearly 10 million cubic metres of wood will have to be marketed, according to a Firca study,” indicated the president of the Fph-CI board of directors, Koblavi-Dibi Michel, who was reporting the results of a Firca study. ; According to him, rubberwood is still under-exploited. “Rubberwood is often used as firewood or charcoal, whereas it can be used to make furniture and many other quality products. A month ago we counted a million rubber trees that have reached the end of their cycle. They are no longer profitable, they must be cut down. They must certainly be sold on the domestic market and exported,” he explained.

a2656.speaker: Firca study (cited)
a2656.name: Firca study (cited)
a2656.speech: A Firca study is cited as the source of the finding that by 2040 nearly 10 million cubic metres of rubberwood will have to be marketed.

a2919.speaker: “What We Know About Exit – Practical Guidance For Developing Exit Strategies in the Field”, C-SAFE Regional Learning Spaces Initiative publication by Alison Gardner, Kara Greenblott and Erika Joubert (an initiative by CARE, World Vision, CRS, ADRA and USAID)
a2919.name: “What We Know About Exit – Practical Guidance For Developing Exit Strategies in the Field”
a2919.title: C-SAFE Regional Learning Spaces Initiative publication by Alison Gardner, Kara Greenblott and Erika Joubert (an initiative by CARE, World Vision, CRS, ADRA and USAID)
a2919.speech: Outlined three basic approaches to Exit Strategies — phasing down, phasing out, and phasing over — and grouped the criteria used to determine when to exit programs into three general categories: time limit, achievement of program impacts, and achievement of benchmarks; recommended implementing exit plans in a gradual, phased manner, since the staggered graduation of project sites can contribute to sustained outcomes, and that continued contact with communities after phase over or phase out helps support sustainability of outcomes; recommended focusing on enhancing community resilience in areas prone to recurrent natural disasters and conducting risk assessments and action plans to mitigate future shocks to food security and livelihoods; suggested contingency plans for various funding scenarios so that a program is not 100% reliant on one donor and keeping staff informed as plans change; and noted challenges including belated planning of an exit strategy, lack of resources and funding restrictions, the need for staff training, high staff turnover, the lack of volunteers and local partners to phase over to, the continued supply of inputs, and limited follow-up capacity, suggesting a staggered exit and soliciting complementary funding for post-project follow-up and evaluation.

a2967.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Finance Minister of Malawi
a2967.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a2967.title: Finance Minister of Malawi
a2967.speech: Announced additional funding Wednesday, taking the 2025-26 budget to K8.076 trillion, including an additional K52 billion allocation towards the Ministry of Health, National Assembly, infrastructure compensation and Millennium Challenge Account top-up resources, National Local Government Finance Committee for blood and blood products, Malawi University of Science and Technology, National Arts and Heritage Council and the Peace and Unity Commission.

a2967.speaker: Sameer Suleman, Blantyre City South East MP
a2967.name: Sameer Suleman
a2967.title: Blantyre City South East MP
a2967.speech: Moved a motion to slash the allocation to State residences from K67 billion to K20 billion in the 2025-26 financial year, in which he wanted the remaining K47 billion to be diverted to the purchase of 1.2 million bags of maize by the Agricultural Development and Marketing Corporation; said it was not ideal to provide State residences with such a budget at a time the country was experiencing hunger ; Described the rejection of his motion as “an injustice” to Malawians and said the MPs had failed Malawians by denying his motion, which he said could have helped the country save taxpayers money: “I feel that the allocation is way too much, considering that this government is only going to be there for the next six months or so. Today, rules were not followed and the welfare of our people is not taken seriously.”

a2967.speaker: Richard Chimwendo Banda, Leader of the House
a2967.name: Richard Chimwendo Banda
a2967.title: Leader of the House
a2967.speech: Said there was no need to reduce the funds as the government had already allocated K60 billion for maize procurement; nevertheless, he agreed that the House go on with the voting process on the matter.

a2967.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Finance Minister of Malawi
a2967.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a2967.title: Finance Minister of Malawi
a2967.speech: Said the government had allocated additional resources to the health sector to ensure that there was continued service delivery on critical services that have been affected by the suspension of aid from the United States of America government, among others: “[We have also set aside] resources for the institutionalisation of key HIV/Aids services, the recruitment and training of frontline health care workers in HIV/Aids service provision, operationalisation of the cancer centre and introduction of dialysis services at Mzuzu Central Hospital.”

a2967.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Finance Minister of Malawi
a2967.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a2967.title: Finance Minister of Malawi
a2967.speech: Said the 2025-26 budget focuses on boosting production of goods and services through agriculture, tourism and mining to address the problem of prolonged imbalance of foreign exchange due to low capacity to export high value goods and services.

a2967.speaker: Ben Phiri, Thyolo Central MP
a2967.name: Ben Phiri
a2967.title: Thyolo Central MP
a2967.speech: Insinuated that 800,000 jobs were lost by December 2024 due to the closure of some companies.

a2967.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Finance Minister of Malawi
a2967.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a2967.title: Finance Minister of Malawi
a2967.speech: Quashed Thyolo Central MP Ben Phiri’s insinuation that 800,000 jobs were lost by December 2024 due to the closure of some companies: “This information, Madam Speaker, is misleading and it does not have any statistical basis. I wish to remind the august House that one of the priorities of the government is creating jobs. Madam Speaker, I therefore wish to encourage those that may be affected by Job losses to engage in other self-employed activities. The substantial support that the government is providing to Neef [National Economic Empowerment Fund] is for such purposes.”

a2967.speaker: Maziko Matemba, Health and Rights Education Programme Executive Director
a2967.name: Maziko Matemba
a2967.title: Health and Rights Education Programme Executive Director
a2967.speech: Has commended Chithyola Banda for providing additional funding towards the health sector.

a2967.speaker: Jappie Mhango, DPP Chief Whip
a2967.name: Jappie Mhango
a2967.title: DPP Chief Whip
a2967.speech: Has said inadequate numbers on the party’s side affected its stand on the budget; according to Mhango, the party’s reservations on the budget failed to be recognised due to the high number of MPs from the government side: “Parliament works on numbers.”

a3184.speaker: Housseini Amion Guindo, former minister and president of the Convergence for the Development of Mali (CODEM)
a3184.name: Housseini Amion Guindo
a3184.title: former minister and president of the Convergence for the Development of Mali (CODEM)
a3184.speech: Paints an alarming picture of the country's situation, pointing to the inability of the transition authorities to respond to the security, political, economic and social challenges, and calls for a national mobilization to avoid the collapse of the country.

a3184.speaker: Housseini Amion Guindo, former minister and president of the Convergence for the Development of Mali (CODEM)
a3184.name: Housseini Amion Guindo
a3184.title: former minister and president of the Convergence for the Development of Mali (CODEM)
a3184.speech: Said the security situation has reached a critical threshold in recent months, with the rise of armed terrorist groups such as JNIM and ISGS and the formation of the Front for the Liberation of Azawad (FLA) aggravating insecurity; also denounces the ineffectiveness of the Disarmament, Demobilization, Reintegration and Integration (DDRI) process, casting doubt on the future of peace in the country.

a3184.speaker: Housseini Amion Guindo, former minister and president of the Convergence for the Development of Mali (CODEM)
a3184.name: Housseini Amion Guindo
a3184.title: former minister and president of the Convergence for the Development of Mali (CODEM)
a3184.speech: Said the transition process is marked by a deficit of dialogue and violations of fundamental freedoms; criticizes the repression of opponents, the dissolution of political parties and associations, and the modification of the transition charter without consultation, practices which he says feed a climate of tension and push away any prospect of an exit from the crisis.

a3184.speaker: Housseini Amion Guindo, former minister and president of the Convergence for the Development of Mali (CODEM)
a3184.name: Housseini Amion Guindo
a3184.title: former minister and president of the Convergence for the Development of Mali (CODEM)
a3184.speech: Points to the economic crisis striking the country, citing excessive dependence on imports, poor governance, the energy crisis and the economic sanctions resulting from Mali's withdrawal from ECOWAS, along with growing social precarity - rising unemployment, galloping inflation and the deterioration of basic social services - and says the situation has become unsustainable for the majority of Malians.

a3184.speaker: Housseini Amion Guindo, former minister and president of the Convergence for the Development of Mali (CODEM)
a3184.name: Housseini Amion Guindo
a3184.title: former minister and president of the Convergence for the Development of Mali (CODEM)
a3184.speech: Faced with what he calls the "rotting of the situation," advocates a national awakening and calls for the creation of an alternative democratic pole bringing together all of the country's vital forces to restore good governance and security; announces the organization of a "national day of anger, indignation and protest" to denounce the failure of the transition and demand a change of course; according to him, only an inclusive approach involving all national actors can allow Mali to emerge durably from this crisis.

a3495.speaker: Spokesperson for the South African government (anonymous)
a3495.name: Spokesperson for the South African government (anonymous)
a3495.speech: "Africa is not a beggar continent. We will no longer be taken for granted. If the US thinks it can just cut off funding and expect us to come crawling back, they are sadly mistaken." ; "We are willing to take a stand and assert our sovereignty. We will no longer be bullied or intimidated by the US."

a3523.speaker: Joan Donoghue, President of the International Court of Justice (ICJ)
a3523.name: Joan Donoghue
a3523.title: President of the International Court of Justice (ICJ)
a3523.speech: Reading the ruling: “By 16 votes to 1, the state of Israel shall take all measures within its power to prevent and punish incitement to commit genocide in relation to members of the Palestinian group in the Gaza strip.” ; “By 15 votes to 2, the state of Israel shall in accordance with its obligations on its convention on the prevention of the crime of genocide, in relation to the Palestinians in Gaza, take all measures within its power to prevent the commission of all acts within its scope of Article 2 of the convention in particular, killing members of the group, causing serious bodily or mental harm to members of the group, deliberately inflicting on the group conditions of life calculated to bring about physical destruction in whole or in part, and indeed imposing measures intending to prevent bursts within the group.”

a3523.speaker: Joan Donoghue, President of the International Court of Justice (ICJ)
a3523.name: Joan Donoghue
a3523.title: President of the International Court of Justice (ICJ)
a3523.speech: Ruled that Israel must allow humanitarian aid into the Strip, saying, “By 16 votes to 1, the state of Israel shall take immediate and effective measures to ensure the provision of urgently needed basic services and humanitarian assistance to address the adverse conditions of life faced by Palestinians in Gaza strip.”

a3523.speaker: Joan Donoghue, President of the International Court of Justice (ICJ)
a3523.name: Joan Donoghue
a3523.title: President of the International Court of Justice (ICJ)
a3523.speech: Said on Friday that South Africa has standing to submit a genocide case against Israel; said “the court concludes that it has jurisdiction to entertain the case,” adding that it “cannot accede to Israel’s request that the case be removed”; noted that both Israel and South Africa are parties to the UN Convention, among other positions.

a3523.speaker: SaharaReporters (earlier report)
a3523.name: SaharaReporters (earlier report)
a3523.speech: SaharaReporters earlier reported that the court ordered Israel to ensure that its forces do not commit genocide and to ensure the preservation of evidence of alleged genocide, and reported earlier that the court ruled that it has jurisdiction to rule in the case filed by South Africa against Israel, alleging genocide in Gaza.

a3589.speaker: Ashok Kumar, Indian High Commissioner to Zambia
a3589.name: Ashok Kumar
a3589.title: Indian High Commissioner to Zambia
a3589.speech: expressed his country's unwavering commitment to supporting Zambia in times of crisis: "I am privileged and honoured to join today's ceremony to present humanitarian assistance of 2,500 metric tonnes of maize on behalf of the people and the government of the Republic of India to the people and..."

a3633.speaker: Local media reports
a3633.name: Local media reports
a3633.speech: Said the joint project works with local governments and communities to strengthen the state's presence and foster a closer relationship between the authorities and citizens; added that the project, funded by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and the German Federal Foreign Office (GFFO), would run till April 2026; explained that the CSSM is implemented in partnership with the International Organization for Migration (IOM), in coordination with Ghana's Ministry of National Security, local government institutions, and community partners. "The project aims to enhance security, promote community cohesion, build the capacity and legitimacy of government institutions, and support social and economic development. It aligns with Ghana's National Framework for the Prevention and Countering of Violent Extremism and Terrorism, focusing on a community-oriented approach to mitigate the spread of Violent Extremist Organizations (VEOs)" ; "The CSSM will also expand to other districts in Ghana's Upper West and Upper East Regions."

a3633.speaker: Anne Witkowsky, U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for Conflict and Stabilization Operations
a3633.name: Anne Witkowsky
a3633.title: U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for Conflict and Stabilization Operations
a3633.speech: Speaking at the launch of the project in Yendi, Northern Region, stressed the importance of reinforcing civilian security in areas vulnerable to violent extremism; said that the project was part of a broader US strategy to prevent conflict and promote stability in coastal West Africa as well as enhancing social cohesion, improving government responsiveness and supporting security across the region.

a3633.speaker: Deike Potzel, German Director General for Crisis Prevention
a3633.name: Deike Potzel
a3633.title: German Director General for Crisis Prevention
a3633.speech: Speaking at the launch of the project in Yendi, Northern Region, stressed the importance of reinforcing civilian security in areas vulnerable to violent extremism.

a3633.speaker: Daniel Krull, German Ambassador to Ghana
a3633.name: Daniel Krull
a3633.title: German Ambassador to Ghana
a3633.speech: Praised Ghana's role as a democratic leader in the region and expressed optimism for free and fair elections in December; reaffirmed the commitment of Germany and the US to strengthen Ghana's resilience against violent extremism and build a more secure and stable future.

a3749.speaker: South Sudanese community leaders at Kakuma camp
a3749.name: South Sudanese community leaders at Kakuma camp
a3749.speech: Told Eye Radio on Monday the situation was tense after the Kenyan police fired live and rubber bullets at the protesting refugees, injuring some individuals.

a3749.speaker: Cornelius Kaka, South Sudanese refugee leader in Kakuma
a3749.name: Cornelius Kaka
a3749.title: South Sudanese refugee leader in Kakuma
a3749.speech: Told Eye Radio that police had dispersed the protestors that morning ; “We went and fought with those people in their office because things are not ok and they refused to give us our rights, they refused to listen to us and the deputy camp manager pushed us by force in using of the police forces” ; “They shot on the person in his stomach and they ran with him because they are using live bullets. Now we are scattered due to the using of the bullets and all this because of the food ratio and refugees refused that.”

a3749.speaker: Kakuma News Reflector, an independent news magazine run by journalists from the camp
a3749.name: Kakuma News Reflector
a3749.title: an independent news magazine run by journalists from the camp
a3749.speech: According to it, thousands of refugees were protesting outside the main entrance of the UN High Commissioner's Sub-Office in Kakuma on March 3, demanding urgent relief for the lack of food, water, and what they describe as unfair treatment.

a3749.speaker: Nation, Kenyan newspaper
a3749.name: Nation
a3749.title: Kenyan newspaper
a3749.speech: Reported that the refugees appeal to the Kenyan government to provide basic necessities or facilitate their return to their home countries; it also indicates that the refugees have voiced concern over the government's plan to integrate them with the Turkana host community, expressing their strong disappointment with the initiative.

a3749.speaker: Simon Ruot, refugee in Kakuma
a3749.name: Simon Ruot
a3749.title: refugee in Kakuma
a3749.speech: Said the humanitarian situation in Kakuma is very dire, adding that the majority of the refugees are close to starvation ; “You know the situation is not good. The strike has now become a threat to the community due to the hunger. Even now, we are still asking people to go back. Yes, we have some gunshots and we are the majority here in Kakuma.”

a3904.speaker: United States Department of Government Efficiency (publication dated 15 February 2025)
a3904.name: United States Department of Government Efficiency (publication dated 15 February 2025)
a3904.speech: Announced that Mali was among the countries that have lost access to American grants, with an envelope of 14 million dollars initially intended for social cohesion projects reportedly cancelled.

a3904.speaker: Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (official statement)
a3904.name: Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (official statement)
a3904.speech: Expressed its surprise at this decision and approached the American authorities to obtain clarification; recalled that Bamako has been warning for several years about the risks of diversion of official development assistance for purposes of destabilisation and the covert financing of terrorist networks.

a3904.speaker: Malian government
a3904.name: Malian government
a3904.speech: Welcomes the American initiative to re-evaluate the use of its grants, considering that this step validates the concerns expressed for a long time by Bamako; urges Washington to go further by initiating legal proceedings against the individuals and structures involved in these diversions.

a3904.speaker: Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a3904.name: Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a3904.speech: Insists on the urgency of identifying and sanctioning those truly responsible for these misappropriations in order to preserve regional stability, noting that Mali and the other member states of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) remain the primary victims of international terrorism and refuse to allow diverted funds to feed these threats.

a3904.speaker: Malian Transition authorities
a3904.name: Malian Transition authorities
a3904.speech: Reaffirm their commitment to pursuing their efforts for peace, sustainable development and social cohesion, while consolidating a model of cooperation founded on mutual respect and national sovereignty.

a4077.speaker: Tanja Pacifico, Head of the IOM mission in Djibouti
a4077.name: Tanja Pacifico
a4077.title: Head of the IOM mission in Djibouti
a4077.speech: Spoke of the cooperation already existing with the CNDH, describing the relationship between the two institutions as "solid and exemplary". She also reaffirmed the importance of the national anchoring of IOM's actions and welcomed the role of independent observer that the CNDH plays in places of detention.

a4077.speaker: IOM team in Djibouti (Tanja Pacifico and colleagues)
a4077.name: IOM team in Djibouti (Tanja Pacifico and colleagues)
a4077.speech: Opened the session by presenting the main activities carried out in Djibouti, highlighting the activities deployed to assist migrants in an irregular situation: humanitarian aid, support for voluntary return, and advocacy for human rights.

a4077.speaker: Ali Mohamed Ali, Vice-President of the National Human Rights Commission (CNDH)
a4077.name: Ali Mohamed Ali
a4077.title: Vice-President of the National Human Rights Commission (CNDH)
a4077.speech: Reported findings from the inspection of the Nagad detention centre that were on the whole reassuring: "We did not notice anything deplorable," and stressed that "human rights conditions were more or less acceptable" ; "Children and women were properly separated from the other candidates for return" ; "Another interesting thing is that we did not see any vulnerable persons."

a4077.speaker: Ali Soubaneh Atteyeh, President of the National Human Rights Commission (CNDH)
a4077.name: Ali Soubaneh Atteyeh
a4077.title: President of the National Human Rights Commission (CNDH)
a4077.speech: In a brief statement, welcomed the progress observed, but also called for the continuation of the reforms needed to guarantee the full dignity of migrants, particularly those in vulnerable situations.

a4077.speaker: CNDH commissioners
a4077.name: CNDH commissioners
a4077.speech: Gave a detailed summary of their inspection conducted the previous day at the Nagad detention centre.

a4077.speaker: CNDH and IOM (joint position at the end of the meeting)
a4077.name: CNDH and IOM (joint position at the end of the meeting)
a4077.speech: Reaffirmed their willingness to cooperate closely in promoting and protecting human dignity, and expressed their joint commitment to promoting the fundamental rights of migrants in accordance with international standards; it was also agreed to strengthen coordination in field operations.

a4229.speaker: US Embassy in Niger (press statement)
a4229.name: US Embassy in Niger (press statement)
a4229.speech: “The nominees for the United States Embassy’s 2024 Nigerien Woman of the Year Prize came from diverse backgrounds. A panel evaluated the nominees on their achievements over the past year, their impact in Niger and their efforts to promote gender equality” ; reported that “Maïmouna Gazibo Gogé is an eminent judge and a graduate of the National School of Administration and Judicial Sciences of Niamey and of the National School of Administration of Strasbourg, France” ; “she is a social activist and a leading human rights defender in Niger. With more than 22,000 followers on Facebook and active engagement through radio, television and in-person presentations, Mrs Gazibo has devoted more than seven years to leading the government agency against human trafficking, begging and prostitution, while fighting gender-based violence, early marriage and gender stigmatisation” ; “Her advocacy uses the legal justice system to fight customary norms that perpetuate human rights violations, and she educates illiterate communities about their rights in local languages” ; “Mrs Gazibo’s work is a testament to her exceptional leadership and her unwavering dedication to the empowerment of underrepresented and vulnerable people in society” ; “This year’s laureate continues to make a considerable positive impact in her community”

a4229.speaker: US Embassy in Niger (press statement)
a4229.name: US Embassy in Niger (press statement)
a4229.speech: Cited “various grants to empower women through the small grants programme of the Public Diplomacy Section, the Special Self-Help Fund of the political and economic section, as well as USAID’s Girls Engage programme and the Trade Hub” ; cited “the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC), which has contributed considerably to the empowerment of Nigerien women by investing 9 million dollars in grants to 86 producer cooperatives, women’s groups, youth associations and enterprises” ; recalled that “since 2008, the MCC has supported the construction of 62 primary schools specifically designed to encourage greater participation of girls in education” while giving the assurance that “USAID Niger is committed to empowering Nigerien women through various initiatives integrated into the education, health and economic sectors” ; recalled that “since January 2022, USAID’s GirlEngage Niger programme has allocated 4.3 million dollars to combat child marriage and promote girls’ education. USAID’s Yalwa grant has enabled many women in Niger to transform their small businesses into thriving veterinary enterprises” ; noted “USAID’s Kulawa project, which supports the Ministry of Public Health by bringing health services closer to underserved populations in the Maradi, Tillabéri and Zinder regions”, recalling that “in 2023 alone, the American government, through USAID, invested more than 8 million dollars to support maternal and child health in Niger”

a4229.speaker: Susan N'Garnim, Chargée d'Affaires of the US Embassy in Niger
a4229.name: Susan N'Garnim
a4229.title: Chargée d'Affaires of the US Embassy in Niger
a4229.speech: Affirmed on this occasion that “the United States Embassy has always supported gender equity and the empowerment of women in Niger.”

a4431.speaker: Yabiladi (Morocco, newspaper report)
a4431.name: Yabiladi (Morocco
a4431.title: newspaper report)
a4431.speech: Highlights the technological breakthrough achieved by inwi, which becomes the first operator in Morocco to introduce routers equipped with WiFi 7 technology, promising performance up to four times higher than current standards, with ultra-fast speeds, low latency and optimised coverage.

a4431.speaker: La Vie Éco (Morocco, newspaper report)
a4431.name: La Vie Éco (Morocco
a4431.title: newspaper report)
a4431.speech: Reports that Managem recorded an 18% rise in its turnover in 2024, reaching 8.86 billion dirhams, explained by rising metal prices, notably gold and silver, and by increased sales volumes from projects in Sudan and Congo, despite the fall in the price of cobalt.

a4431.speaker: El Khabar (Algeria, newspaper report)
a4431.name: El Khabar (Algeria
a4431.title: newspaper report)
a4431.speech: Announces that eight OPEC+ member countries, including Algeria, have agreed to progressively reduce their voluntary oil production limitations starting in April, a decision taken at a virtual meeting aimed at adjusting oil supply to better meet global demand and stabilise energy markets.

a4431.speaker: Le Quotidien (Tunisia, newspaper report)
a4431.name: Le Quotidien (Tunisia
a4431.title: newspaper report)
a4431.speech: Places emphasis on the efforts of TAV Tunisie to improve the performance of the Enfidha and Monastir airports in order to make them more attractive and dynamic platforms.

a4431.speaker: Mélanie Lefebvre, Managing Director of TAV Tunisie
a4431.name: Mélanie Lefebvre
a4431.title: Managing Director of TAV Tunisie
a4431.speech: Stresses the importance of developing these infrastructures to better meet the growing needs of air traffic.

a4431.speaker: Le Temps (Tunisia, newspaper report) / Moody's
a4431.name: Le Temps (Tunisia
a4431.title: newspaper report) / Moody's
a4431.speech: Announces that Moody’s has upgraded Tunisia’s sovereign rating from Caa2 to Caa1, thanks to better management of foreign exchange reserves and historically low current account deficits.

a4431.speaker: Al Marsad (Libya, newspaper report)
a4431.name: Al Marsad (Libya
a4431.title: newspaper report)
a4431.speech: Highlights the political deadlock that continues to delay the presidential elections, with deep disagreements over constitutional reforms and candidate eligibility criteria keeping the country in political instability and stirring growing discontent among the population.

a4431.speaker: Libyan 2 Day (newspaper report)
a4431.name: Libyan 2 Day (newspaper report)
a4431.speech: Reports that the oil company Zueitina Oil has succeeded in restarting a production well in the Al-Sabah field after ten years of shutdown, made possible by securing the site, with an initial capacity of 600 barrels per day.

a4431.speaker: El Fagr (Egypt, newspaper report)
a4431.name: El Fagr (Egypt
a4431.title: newspaper report)
a4431.speech: Highlights the successes of the national “Mashroak” programme, which has financed more than 18,000 projects in Beni Suef province, creating nearly 27,000 jobs in various sectors.

a4431.speaker: Grand Mufti of Egypt (via Egypt Today)
a4431.name: Grand Mufti of Egypt (via Egypt Today)
a4431.speech: Firmly condemned the Israeli decision to block humanitarian aid to Gaza, denouncing a flagrant violation of international law.

a4649.speaker: Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) (statement)
a4649.name: Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) (statement)
a4649.speech: has announced a Balance of Payments (BOP) surplus of $6.83 billion for the 2024 financial year, marking a decisive turnaround from deficits of $3.34 billion in 2023 and $3.32 billion in 2022. “This improvement reflects the impact of wide-ranging macroeconomic reforms, stronger trade performance, and renewed investor confidence in Nigeria’s economy. Stronger Trade and External Account Performance.” It added that the current and capital account recorded a surplus of $17.22 billion in 2024, underpinned by a goods trade surplus of $13.17 billion; petroleum imports declined by 23.2% to $14.06 billion, while non-oil imports fell by 12.6% to $25.74 billion. “On the export side, gas exports rose by 48.3% to $8.66 billion, and non-oil exports increased by 24.6% to $7.46 billion. Remittance inflows remained resilient, with personal remittances rising by 8.9% to $20.93 billion. International Money Transfer Operator (IMTO) inflows surged by 43.5% to $4.73 billion, up from $3.30 billion in 2023, reflecting stronger engagement from the Nigerian diaspora. Official development assistance also rose by 6.2% to $3.37 billion. Improved Financial Account and Reserve Position Nigeria recorded a net acquisition of financial assets totalling $12.12 billion. Portfolio investment inflows more than doubled, increasing by 106.5% to $13.35 billion, while resident foreign currency holdings grew by $5.41 billion, indicating stronger confidence in domestic economic stability. Although foreign direct investment fell by 42.3% to $1.08 billion, the overall financial account posted notable gains. The country’s external reserves increased by $6.0 billion to $40.19 billion by year-end 2024, bolstering its external buffer.”

a4704.speaker: Adanech Abebie, Mayor of Addis Abeba
a4704.name: Adanech Abebie
a4704.title: Mayor of Addis Abeba
a4704.speech: Addressed last week a warm-up session for her party’s upcoming convention, urging cadres of the Prosperity Party - Prosperitians - to embrace what she described as “broad and inclusive” gains ; issues rallying cries to party loyalists in Addis Abeba touting her government’s reforms.

a4704.speaker: Ethiopian policymakers
a4704.name: Ethiopian policymakers
