a4704.speech: Insist these reductions will improve market efficiency and the equitable distribution of resources through targeted social programs; they tout this as part of a pragmatic macroeconomic policy approach.

a4704.speaker: Critics of the Prosperitians
a4704.name: Critics of the Prosperitians
a4704.speech: See the education and health budget cuts as representing a misguided approach, especially in a country struggling to develop its human capital.

a4704.speaker: 2024 Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (report)
a4704.name: 2024 Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (report)
a4704.speech: Notes that Ethiopia remains home to 86 million multidimensionally poor people, amounting to 7.8pc of the global total ; finds that 83.7pc of the world’s multidimensionally poor reside outside urban centres.

a4704.speaker: Unicef
a4704.name: Unicef
a4704.speech: Reported that no less than nine million children remain out of school, driven away by conflict, violence and natural disasters.

a4704.speaker: Ethiopian Economics Association (EEA)
a4704.name: Ethiopian Economics Association (EEA)
a4704.speech: According to the EEA, the Gini coefficient measuring inequality jumped from 32.8pc in 2015/16 to 39.3pc in 2021/22, uncovering that growth, however lauded, has been anything but inclusive.

a4704.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4704.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4704.speech: Projects inflation of 30pc to 35pc this year as a market-determined exchange rate is expected to exacerbate the Birr’s depreciation.

a4704.speaker: Liberalisation advocates
a4704.name: Liberalisation advocates
a4704.speech: Claim the reforms will bring transparency, better governance, and climate-smart investments.

a4753.speaker: Right to Care (health NGO)
a4753.name: Right to Care (health NGO)
a4753.speech: Is calling on men to be circumcised to help prevent cervical cancer, the second most common cancer in women in the country.

a4753.speaker: Dr Khumbulani Moyo, head of the voluntary medical male circumcision programme at Right to Care
a4753.name: Dr Khumbulani Moyo
a4753.title: head of the voluntary medical male circumcision programme at Right to Care
a4753.speech: Said 16 South African women die from cervical cancer every day ; said male circumcision is medically proven to reduce the spread of HIV and STIs such as the HPV by up to 60% ; said persistent infection with HPV, the most common STI, caused cervical cancer, and that the HPV is also the cause of anal, penile, breast and other reproductive organ cancers ; added that while almost all sexually active people would contract the HPV at some point, usually without symptoms, in most cases the immune system cleared the HPV from the body, and persistent infection of the cervix with the high-risk HPV, if left untreated, caused 95% of cervical cancers.

a4753.speaker: Dr Khumbulani Moyo, head of the voluntary medical male circumcision programme at Right to Care
a4753.name: Dr Khumbulani Moyo
a4753.title: head of the voluntary medical male circumcision programme at Right to Care
a4753.speech: Said that a systematic review of 81 published studies provided strong evidence that male circumcision was a powerful tool to reduce women’s risk of cervical cancer, and that research showed that having circumcised male partners substantially lowered the women’s risk of the HPV infection and the development of cervical cancer.

a4753.speaker: Dr Khumbulani Moyo, head of the voluntary medical male circumcision programme at Right to Care
a4753.name: Dr Khumbulani Moyo
a4753.title: head of the voluntary medical male circumcision programme at Right to Care
a4753.speech: Said that medical circumcision was performed under local anaesthetic and took only 30 minutes with very little pain ; addressed concerns some men may have about circumcision affecting their sex life, reassuring that when performed in a medical facility under sterile conditions, circumcision had no adverse effect on sexual function or pleasure.

a4753.speaker: Dr Khumbulani Moyo, head of the voluntary medical male circumcision programme at Right to Care
a4753.name: Dr Khumbulani Moyo
a4753.title: head of the voluntary medical male circumcision programme at Right to Care
a4753.speech: “In addition to encouraging men to undergo circumcision, we also urge women to screen for cervical cancer with a Pap smear or HPV test.”

a4753.speaker: Systematic review of 81 published studies
a4753.name: Systematic review of 81 published studies
a4753.speech: Provided strong evidence that male circumcision was a powerful tool to reduce women’s risk of cervical cancer; research showed that having circumcised male partners substantially lowered the women’s risk of the HPV infection and the development of cervical cancer.

a5051.speaker: State Minister (unnamed), Ethiopian government
a5051.name: State Minister (unnamed)
a5051.title: Ethiopian government
a5051.speech: At a recent workshop, urged young people to master technologies invented in Europe during the early 1900s.

a5051.speaker: World Bank
a5051.name: World Bank
a5051.speech: Estimates that Ethiopia sends nearly two million new job seekers into the labour market each year.

a5051.speaker: Ethiopian Youth Policy of 2004 (policy document)
a5051.name: Ethiopian Youth Policy of 2004 (policy document)
a5051.speech: Pledged to empower individuals aged 15 to 29 by equipping them with skills, knowledge and ethical integrity to participate fully in a democratic system and thrive in economic and social activities; the policy even declared a youth fund, championed by Prime Minister Hailemariam Desalegn.

a5203.speaker: George Mwanza, Mayor of Chipata, Zambia
a5203.name: George Mwanza
a5203.title: Mayor of Chipata, Zambia
a5203.speech: Recounts how, growing up poor in Ngocho, he was able to go to school only because of the benevolence of an uncle, and that witnessing his mother's struggle and suffering after political cadres forcibly seized her land profoundly affected him, leaving him with a growing sense of determination to confront the injustice done to his mother and to many women like her.

a5203.speaker: George Mwanza, Mayor of Chipata, Zambia
a5203.name: George Mwanza
a5203.title: Mayor of Chipata, Zambia
a5203.speech: Explained that his experiences as president of the Junior Engineers, Technicians and Scientists (JETS) club, vice president of the debating club and president of the Youth Development Foundation served to reinforce his belief that he could affect change and inspire others.

a5203.speaker: George Mwanza, Mayor of Chipata, Zambia
a5203.name: George Mwanza
a5203.title: Mayor of Chipata, Zambia
a5203.speech: “My proudest moment is bringing the office of the mayor closer to the people because it is their office and I am the peoples' mayor.” ; “My greatest source of pride lies in bridging the gap between the mayor's office and the people, for it is their office, and I am undeniably the people's mayor.”

a5203.speaker: Alex Ngoma, Zambian political analyst and University of Zambia lecturer
a5203.name: Alex Ngoma
a5203.title: Zambian political analyst and University of Zambia lecturer
a5203.speech: “I think the challenge is that political parties are more rigid in Zambia when it comes to age, this is why they need to have leadership training programmes to train the youth in their ranks. We need more youth leaders. They have more energy and ideas to lead us into the future. We always say young people are the future, but they are also the now, so we need them to be fully involved in leadership.”

a5203.speaker: Alex Ngoma, Zambian political analyst and University of Zambia lecturer
a5203.name: Alex Ngoma
a5203.title: Zambian political analyst and University of Zambia lecturer
a5203.speech: Said Mayor Mwanza's election has heralded a new dawn for Chipata: “The one thing about Mayor Mwanza is that he is proving that young people can do it. He resolved issues at the Chipata City Council, and the town is more vibrant as a result. He is really showing us that young people are capable of leading.”

a5203.speaker: Alex Ngoma, Zambian political analyst and University of Zambia lecturer
a5203.name: Alex Ngoma
a5203.title: Zambian political analyst and University of Zambia lecturer
a5203.speech: “His victory, I think, is part of a bigger movement from around the world. Young people are assuming political seats, so the Zambian political landscape is also changing due to this global change occurring. Young Zambians are seeing their global peers get into political seats, this is encouraging them to vote for each other.”

a5203.speaker: Godfrey Chitalu, Eastern Province Office Manager for the USAID Let's Read project
a5203.name: Godfrey Chitalu
a5203.title: Eastern Province Office Manager for the USAID Let's Read project
a5203.speech: “Mayor George Mwanza serves as an inspiring young leader whose unwavering commitment to education and literacy shines brightly. While the USAID Let's Read Project tirelessly strives to enhance reading proficiency among early-grade students from pre-primary through grade 3, Mayor Mwanza has also been actively involved in supporting local schools by providing them with access to safe drinking water. His contributions include the installation of several boreholes to ensure schools have a reliable water source. Both on a project-wide and personal scale, he has passionately championed the cause of our educational institutions.”

a5341.speaker: Ronald Lamola, South African Minister of International Relations and Co-operation
a5341.name: Ronald Lamola
a5341.title: South African Minister of International Relations and Co-operation
a5341.speech: Says South Africa has no regrets and was fully aware of the consequences of taking Israel to the International Court of Justice (ICJ) for genocide, a move that has strained relations with the US; said the country has no regrets about taking Israel to the ICJ to prevent genocidal acts against Palestinians ; "We can never regret having stood and defended the UN Charter. Even the UN Secretary General continues to champion and support this. As you have seen, even some countries in the West that were critical of South Africa's position are singing the same tune about human rights violations in Gaza and the genocide unfolding. There can't be regrets because any country will accept solidarity when they are under siege."

a5341.speaker: Ronald Lamola, South African Minister of International Relations and Co-operation
a5341.name: Ronald Lamola
a5341.title: South African Minister of International Relations and Co-operation
a5341.speech: Said SA expected there would be consequences as it stood by its principles regarding human rights ; "We knew there would be consequences. Obviously, we will never know the degree, but we also understood at the time and the international community knew, South Africa was vindicating the UN Charter and international human rights law. Obviously, we expected some repercussions, but we expected they would be within the confines of the rules based on international law. The world's biggest superpowers expect you must align with them in one way or the other, but SA's position has always been that we are not anti-Western society, but we stand in our national interest informed by our constitution on human rights and that continues to guide our international (relations)."

a5341.speaker: Ronald Lamola, South African Minister of International Relations and Co-operation
a5341.name: Ronald Lamola
a5341.title: South African Minister of International Relations and Co-operation
a5341.speech: Said SA remained widely respected as a moral compass on the global stage, not only for its case at the ICJ over the war in Gaza but also for its peace interventions across Africa, including in the Democratic Republic of Congo, South Sudan, Ethiopia and Mozambique ; "When everyone was quiet on the issues concerning Gaza, SA stood up and the world continues to respect SA, not only for Gaza but also for its role on the African continent. SA remains highly regarded and respected for its moral standing and for standing firm on its principles."

a5341.speaker: Foreign ministers of France, Canada, Norway, Spain, Australia, New Zealand, Portugal, Ireland, Slovenia, Luxembourg, Malta, Iceland, Andorra and Finland (joint statement)
a5341.name: Foreign ministers of France
a5341.title: Canada, Norway, Spain, Australia, New Zealand, Portugal, Ireland, Slovenia, Luxembourg, Malta, Iceland, Andorra and Finland (joint statement)
a5341.speech: Released a joint statement in July on their intentions to present at the UN General Assembly in September their plans to recognise the Palestinian State, which would have the West Bank as part of its territory, and demanded an immediate ceasefire and the unconditional release of hostages held by Hamas, including the deceased, while also demanding humanitarian aid must be delivered without hindrance.

a5416.speaker: Elijah Ngurare, Prime Minister of Namibia
a5416.name: Elijah Ngurare
a5416.title: Prime Minister of Namibia
a5416.speech: Pledged that the N$371 million budget for the National Planning Commission will be used to support development projects and help the country stay on track to reach its long-term goals under Vision 2030 ; submitted in his budget motivation that the NPC budget for this year will fund key activities, such as tracking the progress of national programmes and strengthening relationships with international development partners ; reflected on some achievements from the 2024/25 year, including completing the National Population and Housing Census and releasing the 2024 Poverty, Vulnerability, and Inequality Report ; “Mobilised Official Development Assistance from various development partners, amounting to N$2.5 billion, which equates to 2.5% of the national budget for the year, is a crucial source of funding that complements the financing of our development programmes.”

a5416.speaker: Elijah Ngurare, Prime Minister of Namibia
a5416.name: Elijah Ngurare
a5416.title: Prime Minister of Namibia
a5416.speech: “Included under this programme is the allocation of a N$60 million development budget for the purchase of the office building for the National Planning Commission.”

a5416.speaker: Elijah Ngurare, Prime Minister of Namibia
a5416.name: Elijah Ngurare
a5416.title: Prime Minister of Namibia
a5416.speech: Asked the National Assembly to approve the budget, as he believes it will help the NPC carry out the country’s development goals.

a5472.speaker: Chinese authorities
a5472.name: Chinese authorities
a5472.speech: Indicated a trend of slight reduction in new infections.

a5472.speaker: Chinese state television
a5472.name: Chinese state television
a5472.speech: Broadcast images of teams spraying disinfectant in streets, residential areas, construction sites and other places where the transmitting mosquitoes might breed in stagnant water.

a5472.speaker: Local authorities (Foshan/Guangdong)
a5472.name: Local authorities (Foshan/Guangdong)
a5472.speech: Threaten to impose fines of up to 10,000 yuan (about 1,200 euros) and electricity cuts on residents who do not eliminate outdoor containers holding water, such as bottles or pots.

a5472.speaker: United States (travel advisory)
a5472.name: United States (travel advisory)
a5472.speech: Issued an advisory discouraging travel to the Chinese province of Guangdong -- where Foshan, Dongguan and other industrial hubs are located -- as well as to countries such as Bolivia, Brazil and island nations of the Indian Ocean, also affected by the virus.

a5778.speaker: Constance Hamilton, Assistant US Trade Representative for Africa
a5778.name: Constance Hamilton
a5778.title: Assistant US Trade Representative for Africa
a5778.speech: Says the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) has failed to meet expected targets since it was launched; said the forum would serve as a stocktaking, through engagements between government officials from across Africa, some members of the US Congress “who hold the pen” on how AGOA should be shaped, as well as civil society, academics and industry captains.

a5778.speaker: US International Trade Commission (April report reviewing AGOA)
a5778.name: US International Trade Commission (April report reviewing AGOA)
a5778.speech: According to the findings, as cited by Hamilton: “One conclusion that they made is that AGOA has not met the expectations we had in 2000, and so while they’re not saying that the programme hasn’t been useful, because some countries have greatly benefited from AGOA, but the majority have not.”

a5778.speaker: Constance Hamilton, Assistant US Trade Representative for Africa
a5778.name: Constance Hamilton
a5778.title: Assistant US Trade Representative for Africa
a5778.speech: Said “And so we know that we still have a lot of work to do,” and that the forum in Johannesburg would be mainly about how to improve AGOA: “After almost 25 years, we know that very few countries are actually taking advantage of this program, and of the sectors that are open and available, very few of those are actually being utilised. So the question I think that’s going to drive the conversation at the AGOA forum in Johannesburg in just a few days is how do we improve on this programme.”

a5778.speaker: Constance Hamilton, Assistant US Trade Representative for Africa
a5778.name: Constance Hamilton
a5778.title: Assistant US Trade Representative for Africa
a5778.speech: Said on Ethiopia’s eligibility: “On the question of Ethiopia’s AGOA eligibility, those decisions are still pending. So no, there probably will not be an announcement at the time that we get to the AGOA Forum.”

a5778.speaker: Joy Basu, Deputy Assistant Secretary, Bureau of African Affairs, US State Department
a5778.name: Joy Basu
a5778.title: Deputy Assistant Secretary, Bureau of African Affairs, US State Department
a5778.speech: Said that while there had been a low uptake, there were cases where AGOA had been utilised to help certain African economies, particularly Angola: “Obviously, there is tremendous potential across - even, for example, just agricultural products that I know are grown in Angola. We have a fantastic ambassador in Angola, Ambassador Mushingi, who really knows the value of economic growth, and that is one of his top priorities in the country.”

a5778.speaker: Joy Basu, Deputy Assistant Secretary, Bureau of African Affairs, US State Department
a5778.name: Joy Basu
a5778.title: Deputy Assistant Secretary, Bureau of African Affairs, US State Department
a5778.speech: Said AGOA principles were directly linked to democracy and human rights: “We remain committed to supporting electoral processes that really deepen democracy across the continent,” ; “So that is relevant in many countries; it’s really a policy focus area of ours as we partner with governments, civil society, and other institutions on the continent.”

a5951.speaker: President Joseph Boakai of Liberia
a5951.name: President Joseph Boakai of Liberia
a5951.speech: Was compelled to declare the evolving drug situation under his regime a “national emergency”.

a5951.speaker: Politicians and activists (unnamed)
a5951.name: Politicians and activists (unnamed)
a5951.speech: Had allowed 2024 to slip without their normal combative and agitative overtures because, in their words, “We are giving the UP one free year of cooling off and to prove itself worthy.”

a6040.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO), message commemorating 2025 World TB Day
a6040.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a6040.title: message commemorating 2025 World TB Day
a6040.speech: Has warned that abrupt cuts in global health funding are threatening progress in the fight against Tuberculosis (TB), the world's deadliest infectious disease ; noted that TB is responsible for over one million deaths annually, bringing devastating impacts on families and communities ; said global efforts to combat TB have saved an estimated 79 million lives since 2000 ; noted that the drastic and abrupt cuts in global health funding are now threatening to reverse these gains ; “Rising drug resistance, especially across Europe, and the ongoing conflicts across the Middle East, Africa, and Eastern Europe, are further exacerbating the situation for the most vulnerable.”

a6040.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a6040.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a6040.speech: Called for an urgent investment of resources to protect and maintain TB care and support services for people in need across regions and countries ; said the theme for the year highlights a rallying cry for urgency, accountability, and hope.

a6040.speaker: 2024 WHO global TB report
a6040.name: 2024 WHO global TB report
a6040.speech: According to the report, an estimated 10.8 million people developed TB in 2023, with 1.6 million people losing their lives and 12 per cent of the global burden affecting the most vulnerable – the children and young adolescents.

a6040.speaker: Tedros Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a6040.name: Tedros Ghebreyesus
a6040.title: WHO Director-General
a6040.speech: Said the huge gains the world has made against TB over the past 20 years are now at risk as cuts to funding start to disrupt access to services for prevention, screening, and treatment for people with TB ; said the WHO is committed to working with all donors, partners and affected countries to mitigate the impact of funding cuts and find innovative solutions ; “We cannot give up on the concrete commitments that world leaders made at the UN General Assembly just 18 months ago to accelerate work to end TB.”

a6040.speaker: Tedros Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a6040.name: Tedros Ghebreyesus
a6040.title: WHO Director-General
a6040.speech: Noted that early reports revealed severe TB response disruptions are seen across several of the highest-burden countries following the funding cuts, with countries in the WHO African Region experiencing the greatest impact, followed by the South-East Asian and Western Pacific Regions ; “27 countries are facing crippling breakdowns in their TB response, with devastating consequences, such as human resource shortages undermining service delivery; diagnostic services severely disrupted, delaying detection and treatment; data and surveillance systems collapsing, compromising disease tracking and management” ; “Others affected are community engagement efforts, including active case finding, screening, and contact tracing, deteriorating, leading to delayed diagnoses and increased transmission risks” ; said nine countries report failing TB drug procurement and supply chains, jeopardising treatment continuity and patient outcomes.

a6040.speaker: Tereza Kasaeva, Director of WHO's Global Programme on TB and Lung Health
a6040.name: Tereza Kasaeva
a6040.title: Director of WHO's Global Programme on TB and Lung Health
a6040.speech: “This urgent call is timely and underscores the necessity of swift, decisive action to sustain global TB progress and prevent setbacks that could cost lives” ; said investing in ending TB is not only a moral imperative but also an economic necessity, as every dollar spent on prevention and treatment yields an estimated $43 in economic returns.

a6040.speaker: WHO Director-General and Civil Society Task Force on Tuberculosis
a6040.name: WHO Director-General and Civil Society Task Force on Tuberculosis
a6040.speech: Demand immediate, coordinated efforts from governments, global health leaders, donors, and policymakers to prevent further disruptions.

a6061.speaker: Sekai Nzenza, Zimbabwe Industry Minister
a6061.name: Sekai Nzenza
a6061.title: Zimbabwe Industry Minister
a6061.speech: has said Zimbabwe is creating bilateral relations with other countries in the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) to improve its competitiveness and productivity ; speaking during a Global Federation of Competitiveness Councils’ (GFCC) virtual meeting last week, the minister said it was imperative for Zimbabwe to learn from the best.

a6067.speaker: Zimplow (company trading update)
a6067.name: Zimplow (company trading update)
a6067.speech: says its sales volumes of local agricultural machinery under its Mealie Brand subsidiary improved by 70 percent in comparison to the prior year.

a6067.speaker: Vimbayi Nyakudya, Zimplow chief executive
a6067.name: Vimbayi Nyakudya
a6067.title: Zimplow chief executive
a6067.speech: in a trading update for the five-month period ending May 31, 2023, said sales volumes for the export market had reduced by 38 percent.

a6108.speaker: United States diplomatic mission in Washington (US Embassy)
a6108.name: United States diplomatic mission in Washington (US Embassy)
a6108.speech: Announced that American diplomat Duke Buchan was officially sworn in on Monday 14 October as United States Ambassador to Morocco; in a statement released on Wednesday, the American embassy indicated that Mr Buchan "looks forward to joining Rabat soon in order to advance and deepen the long-standing partnership between the United States and Morocco."

a6108.speaker: United States and Morocco (both countries)
a6108.name: United States and Morocco (both countries)
a6108.speech: Describe the alliance between them as a "historic strategic partnership."

a6108.speaker: American diplomacy (US State Department)
a6108.name: American diplomacy (US State Department)
a6108.speech: Said his taking up of duties will occur before the end of October, underlining "the importance of Morocco's role as a pillar of stability and dialogue in the region."

a6113.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria (then APC presidential aspirant)
a6113.name: Bola Tinubu
a6113.title: President of Nigeria (then APC presidential aspirant)
a6113.speech: In obvious allusion to the overt plots against him at the time, an exasperated Tinubu told a crowd of supporters in Ogun State that it was his turn to be President. He captured this in Yoruba as "emi lokan."

a6113.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria (then APC presidential candidate)
a6113.name: Bola Tinubu
a6113.title: President of Nigeria (then APC presidential candidate)
a6113.speech: Advocated the recruitment of "50 million youths" to fight ravaging insurgency and banditry across the land; they would be fed with "garri, ewa, agbado," (cassava grains, beans and maize), was his prescription at the time.

a6113.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria (then APC presidential candidate)
a6113.name: Bola Tinubu
a6113.title: President of Nigeria (then APC presidential candidate)
a6113.speech: At an event in Owerri in the South East as part of his campaigns, trailed off his script and spoke about "a town-hall different from balablu blublu bulaba," which was not captured in his prepared text.

a6131.speaker: Teguest Yilma, National Polio Plus Committee deputy chair
a6131.name: Teguest Yilma
a6131.title: National Polio Plus Committee deputy chair
a6131.speech: Stressed that Polio should be the second disease eradicated in history ; “It is an extraordinary success for Ethiopia to achieve polio free status and it allows us to look ahead with great joy towards Polio endgame projects” ; “Still, we realize that now is not the time to rest, as the danger is lurking around. The status of Ethiopia as non-infected with Polio is threatened with the existence of the virus in neighboring countries like Somalia.”

a6131.speaker: Delegates from Core Group, Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, CDC, USAID, UNICEF and WHO
a6131.name: Delegates from Core Group
a6131.title: Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, CDC, USAID, UNICEF and WHO
a6131.speech: Addressed the attendees of the conference. They reiterated the need to raise awareness against Polio and to unite communities to fight it emphasizing the necessity to increase joint efforts from all health partners to stem the spread of polio virus.

a6131.speaker: Joint statement between UNICEF, Rotary and WHO
a6131.name: Joint statement between UNICEF
a6131.title: Rotary and WHO
a6131.speech: Noted two simultaneous potential outbreaks in the Horn of Africa due to vaccine-derived poliovirus. Outbreaks of vaccine-derived poliovirus can be stopped in the same way as wild polio by vaccinating every child, according to the statement ; “The Governments of Somalia, Kenya and Ethiopia, as well as countries across the Horn of Africa, are committed to working together to stop the outbreaks as soon as possible.”

a6266.speaker: IDMC report (released Monday)
a6266.name: IDMC report (released Monday)
a6266.speech: Stresses that the current number of internally displaced people is equivalent to the population of Germany and is more than double the figure recorded six years ago ; stresses that in many situations people had to flee several times over the course of the year, as conflict areas shifted, increasing their vulnerabilities and impeding their efforts to rebuild their lives.

a6266.speaker: Alexandra Bilak, Director of the IDMC
a6266.name: Alexandra Bilak
a6266.title: Director of the IDMC
a6266.speech: “Internal displacement happens where conflict, poverty and the complications of climate exist, hitting the most vulnerable hardest” ; “These figures prove that internal displacement is not only a humanitarian crisis. It is a clear political and development challenge that requires far more attention than it currently receives.”

a6266.speaker: IDMC analysis (released today)
a6266.name: IDMC analysis (released today)
a6266.speech: According to the analysis, almost 90% of internally displaced people, that is, 73.5 million people, were displaced by conflict and violence, an 80% increase in six years; disasters provoked 45.8 million internal displacements last year, the highest annual number since the IDMC began monitoring disaster displacement in 2008; weather-related events triggered 99.5% of disaster displacements; the analysis notes that displacement can also be a positive mechanism in disaster-prone countries, as with preventive evacuations in the US, the Philippines or Bangladesh.

a6266.speaker: Jan Egeland, Secretary-General of the Norwegian Refugee Council
a6266.name: Jan Egeland
a6266.title: Secretary-General of the Norwegian Refugee Council
a6266.speech: Quoted in the document saying the figures recorded in 2024 should serve as a warning about the state of global solidarity ; “Internal displacement rarely makes headlines, but for those who live it, the suffering can last for years,” asking “how much longer the number of people affected by the lack of accountability and leadership can keep growing” ; stressed that every time humanitarian aid funding is cut, one more displaced person loses access to food, medicine, security and hope ; “Over the past year, I met internally displaced families in the Democratic Republic of Congo, in Palestine and in Sudan, and I heard them speak about the devastating impact of displacement on their lives and about their hopes for the future”; for whom the lack of progress is both a political failure and a moral stain on humanity ; “Now is the moment for governments to demonstrate political will and financial investment to find durable solutions that help the displaced.”

a6266.speaker: IDMC
a6266.name: IDMC
a6266.speech: Concedes that the number of preventive-evacuation displacements may even have been higher since there is no complete data on these situations.

a6266.speaker: Alexandra Bilak, Director of the IDMC
a6266.name: Alexandra Bilak
a6266.title: Director of the IDMC
a6266.speech: “The data are clear” ; “Now is the time to use them to prevent displacement, support recovery and build resilience. Immediate efforts are needed to help the people who have lost everything, and investment to deal with the underlying vulnerabilities in order to avoid it.”

a6315.speaker: International Cospas-Sarsat Organisation (announcement at virtual meeting of 13 June)
a6315.name: International Cospas-Sarsat Organisation (announcement at virtual meeting of 13 June)
a6315.speech: Announced the creation of an international working group specialising in artificial intelligence applications in search-and-rescue satellite systems, following the 27th round of meetings held in Abu Dhabi from 5 May to 2 June 2025.

a6315.speaker: UAE National Guard Command, represented by the National Search and Rescue Centre (working paper)
a6315.name: UAE National Guard Command
a6315.title: represented by the National Search and Rescue Centre (working paper)
a6315.speech: Submitted the working paper on which the decision is based, at the meetings of the International Committee attended by representatives from 45 countries as well as the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) and the International Maritime Organisation (IMO); the UAE put forward an advanced technical proposal aimed at integrating artificial intelligence technologies into the operations of the Mission Control Centre (MCC), increasing the effectiveness of space-based rescue systems, and increasing the speed and accuracy of responses to distress calls through intelligent data processing and integration between satellite networks.

a6315.speaker: COSPAS-SARSAT member states
a6315.name: COSPAS-SARSAT member states
a6315.speech: Gave the UAE initiative wide praise for its innovative and forward-looking approach, reflecting the country's readiness and leadership in supporting international efforts to modernise the technical infrastructure of the COSPAS-SARSAT system; a recommendation was adopted to create a joint working group under UAE chairmanship to coordinate technical cooperation among member states and relevant bodies and to develop artificial intelligence tools linked to mission control centres.

a6315.speaker: International Committee on Artificial Intelligence in Search and Rescue Systems
a6315.name: International Committee on Artificial Intelligence in Search and Rescue Systems
a6315.speech: Highly commended the UAE's role, its quality contribution and its active initiatives in applying modern technologies to serve international humanitarian rescue objectives.

a6433.speaker: Jan Wahlberg, Finland's Ambassador for Mediation
a6433.name: Jan Wahlberg
a6433.title: Finland's Ambassador for Mediation
a6433.speech: Emphasized Finland's commitment in his speech at the launch, stating, "Finnish youth played an active role when the UN Security Council drafted the Youth, Peace, and Security resolution in 2015. Finnish youth handed a petition on this matter to then-Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon. It is worth noting that Finland was the first country in the world to create a national action plan to implement the Youth, Peace, and Security resolution."

a6433.speaker: Mohamed Barre Mohamud, Somalia's Minister for Youth and Sports
a6433.name: Mohamed Barre Mohamud
a6433.title: Somalia's Minister for Youth and Sports
a6433.speech: Stressed the high unemployment rates and the resulting despair among young people in the Horn of Africa ; noted that youth under 25 make up 60% of Africa's population, yet their potential contributions to development and peace are often overlooked.

a6433.speaker: Mohamed Barre Mohamud, Somalia's Minister for Youth and Sports
a6433.name: Mohamed Barre Mohamud
a6433.title: Somalia's Minister for Youth and Sports
a6433.speech: "As the Minister of Youth, I am committed to achieving positive changes by promoting policies and advocating for their rights. Through initiatives like Youth Skills for Peace and Somalia's Youth Policy 2023-2030, we are laying the foundation for youth to actively participate in processes aimed at creating peace and security in Somalia. I am proud to announce that the Somali Ministry of Youth and Sports has prioritized youth, peace, and security by making it the fourth pillar of our national policy."

a6433.speaker: Suldaan Said Ahmed, Special Representative of the Finnish Foreign Minister for the Horn of Africa
a6433.name: Suldaan Said Ahmed
a6433.title: Special Representative of the Finnish Foreign Minister for the Horn of Africa
a6433.speech: Shared his experiences from recent official peace missions to the region, highlighting hopeful developments that require youth involvement to ensure long-term stability.

a6433.speaker: Laura Järvilehto, communications specialist for the international operations of the Helsinki Deaconess Foundation
a6433.name: Laura Järvilehto
a6433.title: communications specialist for the international operations of the Helsinki Deaconess Foundation
a6433.speech: Presented the Foundation's peace work at the event, including creating employment opportunities for young people, which is integral to peace-building efforts ; announced that Suldaan Said Ahmed will coordinate the East African Youth Peace Network on behalf of the Deaconess Foundation, which will also oversee the network administratively ; added, "The network's goals and methods of operation will be planned in subsequent meetings."

a6433.speaker: Jamila Mohamud, member of the East African Youth Peace Network
a6433.name: Jamila Mohamud
a6433.title: member of the East African Youth Peace Network
a6433.speech: "We have grown up in a safe country (Finland), so it is time to bring peace to our homeland, from which we or our parents moved away due to insecurity. The youth peace network is expected to inspire many young people who are interested in peace work both internationally and here in Finland."

a6433.speaker: Bilal Mohammed Hussein, member of the East African Youth Peace Network
a6433.name: Bilal Mohammed Hussein
a6433.title: member of the East African Youth Peace Network
a6433.speech: Emphasized the crucial role of youth in these initiatives: "Youth are the future, and their opinions must be heard in peace processes. The first impression I have gotten from this network is that I really have the opportunity to be involved in planning and then implementing peace-related activities."

a6615.speaker: Group of Tunisian members of parliament of the Assembly of the Representatives of the People (ARP) (joint statement)
a6615.name: Group of Tunisian members of parliament of the Assembly of the Representatives of the People (ARP) (joint statement)
a6615.speech: Forcefully denounced the "criminal abduction" of their colleague Mohamed Ali, arrested with other members of the global Soumoud flotilla as they were heading to Gaza to deliver humanitarian aid, describing the operation carried out by Israeli forces as a "flagrant violation of international law and humanitarian law." According to them, this arrest constitutes not only an infringement of freedom of movement and of humanitarian action, but also "a direct attack on a sovereign institution embodying the will of the Tunisian people."

a6615.speaker: Group of Tunisian members of parliament of the Assembly of the Representatives of the People (ARP) (joint statement)
a6615.name: Group of Tunisian members of parliament of the Assembly of the Representatives of the People (ARP) (joint statement)
a6615.speech: The parliamentarians demand the immediate and unconditional release of the deputy and of all those arrested aboard the vessel. They hold Israel "entirely responsible" for the safety of Tunisian citizens, considering that this act represents a provocation toward the Tunisian people as a whole.

a6615.speaker: Group of Tunisian members of parliament of the Assembly of the Representatives of the People (ARP) (joint statement)
a6615.name: Group of Tunisian members of parliament of the Assembly of the Representatives of the People (ARP) (joint statement)
a6615.speech: The signatories call for a firm national response and request that an extraordinary session of parliament be held. They also propose the establishment of an emergency commission to coordinate with the Tunisian authorities and international organisations with a view to securing the rapid release of the detainees. ; Finally, the deputies urge the international community, foreign parliaments and human rights organisations to condemn these "abuses" and to intervene to guarantee the protection of the flotilla's participants.

a6626.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a6626.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a6626.title: Ukrainian President
a6626.speech: Urged Switzerland to allow the re-export of weapons to Ukraine, saying the move would be vital in defeating Russia's invasion: "I know there is a discussion in Switzerland about the exportation of war materiel to protect and defend Ukraine. That would be vital," ; "We need weapons so we can restore peace in Ukraine." ; thanked Switzerland for adopting EU sanctions over the invasion but said more was needed.

a6626.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a6626.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a6626.title: Ukrainian President
a6626.speech: In his speech, invited Switzerland to host a global peace summit on Ukraine. He said he had spoken to Swiss President Alain Berset about the initiative in March.

a6626.speaker: Swiss home affairs ministry (headed by Alain Berset)
a6626.name: Swiss home affairs ministry (headed by Alain Berset)
a6626.speech: There was no immediate comment from home affairs ministry, headed up by Berset.

a6626.speaker: Swiss People's Party (SVP)
a6626.name: Swiss People's Party (SVP)
a6626.speech: Snubbed the speech, saying it was in violation of the country's neutrality.

a6810.speaker: Peter Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a6810.name: Peter Vrooman
a6810.title: US Ambassador to Mozambique
a6810.speech: reiterates that US support for essential projects in the country will not be affected, despite the difficulties faced. “You know that some projects are in a paused situation, but we have exemptions for some life-saving projects, that is, PEPFAR projects [the US President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief], antiretrovirals and also logistics for the health sector, and we are going to continue our programmes to save the lives of two million Mozambicans who have HIV,” Vrooman said. The ambassador stressed that “we work with partners here such as the Government and the private sector and also NGOs, to safeguard these humanitarian assistance programmes.”

a6810.speaker: Peter Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a6810.name: Peter Vrooman
a6810.title: US Ambassador to Mozambique
a6810.speech: “We also have projects in the area of humanitarian assistance, and this also continues,” said Ambassador Vrooman, referring to joint work with national and international partners to ensure the continuity of aid initiatives ; he stressed during the meeting that continued US support is a crucial step towards ensuring a “stronger, safer and more prosperous” future.

a6810.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS
a6810.name: Winnie Byanyima
a6810.title: Executive Director of UNAIDS
a6810.speech: acknowledged the country’s progress, saying that “Mozambique has made a lot of progress, reducing new infections and reducing deaths.” However, she also stressed that the challenge persists, since “Mozambique has two million people who are in treatment, 400,000 still to be brought into treatment, 80,000 new infections every year, so it keeps growing.”

a6810.speaker: Official data (Mozambique)
a6810.name: Official data (Mozambique)
a6810.speech: Official data indicate that 2.4 million people live with HIV in the country, reinforcing the importance of continuing treatment and prevention programmes.

a6846.speaker: Tanzania Digest (report)
a6846.name: Tanzania Digest (report)
a6846.speech: Says the accolade is more than just a personal honour — it recognizes her empathetic and visionary leadership, which has guided Tanzania toward stability, progress, and global recognition ; “As a leader, President Samia inspires hope and change, reminding us of the power of integrity, unity, and collaboration in governance” ; “President Samia has consistently demonstrated an empathetic and visionary leadership style. Her ability to navigate complex political, economic, and social landscapes has positioned Tanzania as a beacon of stability and progress in the region.” ; says the honour bestowed upon her by Mzumbe University carries profound significance — it is a tribute from an institution that shaped her formative years, acknowledging her transformative impact on national and global governance ; “This act of humility underscores her belief in shared success and her deep commitment to servant leadership. Her words resonate as a reminder that no achievement is ever truly individual; it results from collaboration, trust, and a shared vision for a better future.” ; “Mzumbe University’s decision to recognise President Samia reflects her extraordinary contributions to Tanzania’s development. From championing economic reforms to advocating for women’s empowerment and steering Tanzania’s diplomatic relations to new heights, her leadership embodies resilience and innovation. She has shown the world that governance rooted in integrity and inclusivity can yield transformative results.” ; “This honorary degree is not just a personal accolade for President Samia; it symbolizes the progress of a nation under her guidance. Her tenure has been marked by bold reforms, fostering a culture of accountability, and prioritizing the well-being of all citizens. She has inspired millions with her poise, intellect, and steadfast dedication to service, breaking barriers and setting a new standard for leadership in Africa and beyond.” ; “As Tanzanians, this recognition calls upon us to reflect on the significance of having a leader who understands the intricacies of governance and embodies the values of compassion, unity, and progress. It is a call to rally behind her vision and collectively contribute to the sustainable development of our beloved nation.”

a6846.speaker: President Samia Suluhu Hassan of Tanzania
a6846.name: President Samia Suluhu Hassan of Tanzania
a6846.speech: In her heartfelt remarks, graciously dedicated the award to all Tanzanians and the collective efforts of those who have supported her leadership journey.

a6846.speaker: Tanzania Digest (report on Tanzania’s G20 invitation)
a6846.name: Tanzania Digest (report on Tanzania’s G20 invitation)
a6846.speech: Explores how the East African country can leverage its G20 presence to advance critical national interests and strengthen its leadership role in Africa’s development, arguing that Tanzania should translate the recognition into increased foreign direct investments, trade agreements and development projects; advocate for equitable growth on behalf of the continent alongside South Africa and the African Union on food security, debt relief and renewable energy; advocate for climate-resilient agriculture, renewable energy and inclusive technological access; balance foreign investment in rare earth minerals with national interests through transparent legal frameworks and sustainable mining; invest in reducing post-harvest losses and strengthening local value chains; link G20 commitments to Vision 2025; diversify economic partnerships through South-South cooperation because over-reliance on foreign aid risks undermining Tanzania’s sovereignty and long-term growth; champion gender equity; implement robust monitoring and evaluation mechanisms; and strengthen collaboration with the African Union to amplify Africa’s collective voice.

a6846.speaker: Tanzania Digest (report)
a6846.name: Tanzania Digest (report)
a6846.speech: Concludes by saying: “Under President Samia’s visionary leadership, strategic engagement can attract investments, forge transformative partnerships, and address critical challenges such as climate change and food security.” ; “This moment demands a commitment to turning global promises into actionable change, ensuring a legacy of progress and prosperity for Tanzania and Africa at large.”

a6941.speaker: World Bank (announcement/press release)
a6941.name: World Bank (announcement/press release)
a6941.speech: Announced that it has approved additional International Development Association (IDA) financing of 100 million dollars to support Mali and Chad, with each country receiving 50 million dollars, to be used in Chad to strengthen the initial activities of the Integrated Flood Control and Urban Resilience Project in N'Djamena (PILIER) and in Mali to replenish the Bamako Urban Resilience Project (PRUBA) after the activation of its Contingent Emergency Response Component for 73 million dollars immediately after the floods.

a6941.speaker: Clara De Sousa, World Bank division director
a6941.name: Clara De Sousa
a6941.title: World Bank division director
a6941.speech: "The speed with which the two additional financings were mobilized testifies to the World Bank's readiness to respond adequately to the scale of the needs of Mali and Chad, which were severely affected by the 2024 floods." ; "This intervention is part of the strengthening of our emergency response and disaster resilience in the Sahel region, which is fully exposed to the inexorable changes of the climate."

a6993.speaker: Reporters Without Borders (RSF)
a6993.name: Reporters Without Borders (RSF)
a6993.speech: Reports that since the new US leader assumed the presidency he “announced the freezing of US foreign aid, and USAID (the United States Agency for International Development) is in turmoil: the website is inaccessible, the account on X suspended, the agency's headquarters closed and staff instructed to stay at home.”

a6993.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a6993.name: Elon Musk
a6993.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a6993.speech: Insinuated that USAID was a “criminal organisation,” although the agency is present in more than 30 countries.

a6993.speaker: News organisations around the world (via RSF)
a6993.name: News organisations around the world (via RSF)
a6993.speech: Contacted RSF “expressing confusion, chaos and uncertainty,” following Trump's announcements, which affect international NGOs such as the International Fund for Public Interest Media and media outlets that live under repressive conditions.

a6993.speaker: Clayton Weimers, executive director of RSF USA
a6993.name: Clayton Weimers
a6993.title: executive director of RSF USA
a6993.speech: “President Trump justified this order by accusing - without evidence - the so-called 'foreign aid industry' of not being aligned with US interests.”

a6993.speaker: USAID information taken offline in 2023 (agency data cited by RSF)
a6993.name: USAID information taken offline in 2023 (agency data cited by RSF)
a6993.speech: “According to USAID information taken offline in 2023, the agency funded training and support for 6,200 journalists, assisted 707 non-state media outlets and supported 279 media-sector civil society organisations.”

a6993.speaker: An exiled Belarusian journalist (anonymous)
a6993.name: An exiled Belarusian journalist (anonymous)
a6993.speech: “We have articles scheduled until the end of January, but after that, if we do not find solutions, we will not be able to publish any more.”

a6993.speaker: An exiled Iranian journalist (anonymous)
a6993.name: An exiled Iranian journalist (anonymous)
a6993.speech: Warns that the impact of the funding freeze could silence the last remaining free voices, creating a vacuum that Iranian state propaganda would inevitably fill: “Switching us off will mean that they have more power.”

a6993.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a6993.name: Marco Rubio
a6993.title: US Secretary of State
a6993.speech: “Announced that he had been appointed acting director of the agency [USAID], suggesting that its operations were being transferred to the State Department.”

a7045.speaker: Lingalireni Mihowa, Oxfam in Malawi country director
a7045.name: Lingalireni Mihowa
a7045.title: Oxfam in Malawi country director
a7045.speech: Observed that restructuring the social protection programmes to move from just consumption could be key. She said: “It is important to protect the most vulnerable and poor, but there is need to design the programmes that have exit strategies, have sustainability pathways and those that are linked to production and stimulating local economies, not just consumption. There is need to limit consumption to marginalised groups who cannot offer labour for cash such as the elderly and children.”

a7045.speaker: Oxfam in Malawi
a7045.name: Oxfam in Malawi
a7045.speech: Has called for restructuring of social protection programmes to have an exit strategy in view of the economic distress and shocks the country continues to face.

a7045.speaker: Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs (data)
a7045.name: Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs (data)
a7045.speech: Data shows that on average, Malawi Government has been contributing five percent to the funding of the Social Cash Transfer Programme (SCTP) since 2016/17 fiscal year, with 36 percent of resources coming from the World Bank, 27 percent from Germany, 23 percent from the European Union (EU), seven percent from Irish Aid and one percent technical support from United Nations’ Children Fund.

a7045.speaker: Agness Nyirongo, Centre for Social Concern economic governance officer
a7045.name: Agness Nyirongo
a7045.title: Centre for Social Concern economic governance officer
a7045.speech: Said government funding is not enough to shield the programme from external financial shocks. “While the financing arrangement has allowed the programme to scale up rapidly, it also exposes it to serious risks, especially now that foreign aid to Malawi and many other low-income countries is becoming increasingly uncertain,” he said.

a7045.speaker: Cassim
a7045.name: Cassim
a7045.speech: Said macroeconomic instability reduces the real value of the cash transfers, undermining its effectiveness. “Without clear pathways for economically active households to move out of the programme, there is a risk of long-term dependency,” he said.

a7045.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, Scotland-based Malawian economist
a7045.name: Velli Nyirongo
a7045.title: Scotland-based Malawian economist
a7045.speech: Said in an interview yesterday that the country faces limited resources, high poverty rates and rapid population growth, which put significant pressure on public finances.

a7045.speaker: Ministry of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare
a7045.name: Ministry of Gender
a7045.title: Community Development and Social Welfare
a7045.speech: Hopes to increase the coverage for the programme to 15 percent between 2022 and 2027 as outlined in the strategic plan.

a7280.speaker: German Federal Foreign Office (press statement extended to Eye Radio)
a7280.name: German Federal Foreign Office (press statement extended to Eye Radio)
a7280.speech: Said the shifting of diplomatic operations from South Sudan is not a permanent decision: "This is not a permanent decision but rather a temporary measure. As soon as conditions permit, the Embassy will resume its operations in Juba." ; also posted a statement on X (formerly known as Twitter) confirming the decision.

a7280.speaker: German Federal Foreign Office (press statement extended to Eye Radio)
a7280.name: German Federal Foreign Office (press statement extended to Eye Radio)
a7280.speech: Added that it remains steadfastly on the side of the South Sudanese people: "We support their endeavor for a peaceful and prosperous future as one of the largest donors both in terms of humanitarian assistance and development cooperation, totaling more than 300 million Euros."

a7280.speaker: Annalena Baerbock, German Minister of Foreign Affairs
a7280.name: Annalena Baerbock
a7280.title: German Minister of Foreign Affairs
a7280.speech: Called upon President Kiir and First Vice President Machar to prevent a further escalation of violence and to implement the peace agreement of 2018.

a7280.speaker: Local authorities (South Sudan)
a7280.name: Local authorities (South Sudan)
a7280.speech: According to local authorities, the government's response to the conflict in Nasir with aerial bombardment has left dozens dead.

a7321.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, President of Namibia
a7321.name: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah
a7321.title: President of Namibia
a7321.speech: Has urged all Namibians to reject divisive tendencies such as tribalism, regionalism, and discrimination in order to build a unified and inclusive society.

a7321.speaker: Kaweche Kaunda, son of Zambia's founding President Kenneth Kaunda
a7321.name: Kaweche Kaunda
a7321.title: son of Zambia's founding President Kenneth Kaunda
a7321.speech: As Namibia celebrates its 36th Independence celebrations, has cautioned Namibians not to fall into the trap of division.

a7321.speaker: Alick Banda, Archbishop of the Cosmopolitan Archdiocese of Lusaka, Zambia
a7321.name: Alick Banda
a7321.title: Archbishop of the Cosmopolitan Archdiocese of Lusaka, Zambia
a7321.speech: Appeared before the Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC) for questioning but opted to remain silent.

a7321.speaker: Mulilo Kabesha, Attorney General of Zambia
a7321.name: Mulilo Kabesha
a7321.title: Attorney General of Zambia
a7321.speech: Has demanded access to the late Edgar Lungu's body for identification and authentication purposes, and, through the lawyers representing the state in South Africa, has warned that failure to grant access will prompt them to seek an order from the Pretoria High Court.

a7321.speaker: Nellie Mutti, Speaker of the National Assembly of Zambia
a7321.name: Nellie Mutti
a7321.title: Speaker of the National Assembly of Zambia
a7321.speech: Has ordered that the daughter of the late former Zambian President Edgar Lungu, Tasila Lungu, an elected Member of Parliament, should appear before her office 14 days after the burial of her father; failure to do so would see her lose her seat.

a7321.speaker: Mutale Nalumango, Vice President of Zambia
a7321.name: Mutale Nalumango
a7321.title: Vice President of Zambia
a7321.speech: In the Zambian Parliament's debate on the late Edgar Lungu's funeral impasse, called on the family to take charge.

a7347.speaker: Government of Mozambique
a7347.name: Government of Mozambique
a7347.speech: insists it must distribute humanitarian assistance in Palma, but has no system to do so.

a7347.speaker: Roque Silva, Frelimo Secretary General
a7347.name: Roque Silva
a7347.title: Frelimo Secretary General
a7347.speech: said in Quitunda, the resettlement town at the gates of Afungi, that Frelimo was giving 20 tonnes of food.

a7347.speaker: Private businesses sending food to Palma
a7347.name: Private businesses sending food to Palma
a7347.speech: said the 20 tonnes had been taken from their 100 tonne delivery.

a7347.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) and other aid agencies
a7347.name: World Food Programme (WFP) and other aid agencies
a7347.speech: They insist on doing their own distribution; they have been ready to send food and other essentials to Palma for two weeks, but cannot obtain agreement, and the apparent disappearance of the 100 tonnes and the realisation that INGD has no distribution system has made them even more anxious about releasing aid to the military or a government agency.

a7347.speaker: One business person (unnamed)
a7347.name: One business person (unnamed)
a7347.speech: stressed the priority is to get food and medicines into Palma. They said there was a need for mutual “respect” – people distributing food would be given “respect” in exchange for showing “respect” for the local authorities – Frelimo and the defence forces.

a7347.speaker: Civilians in Palma
a7347.name: Civilians in Palma
a7347.speech: claim they are harassed and even shot or disappeared by the FDS, which distrusts all local people.

a7347.speaker: Insurgents (al Shabaab) in Palma
a7347.name: Insurgents (al Shabaab) in Palma
a7347.speech: have told local people in Palma that they will not attack during the month of Ramadan, which ends on 12 May, but they predict another attack after that.

a7347.speaker: Total (company statement, Paris headquarters)
a7347.name: Total (company statement
a7347.title: Paris headquarters)
a7347.speech: declared “force majeure” on its Mozambique LNG project, due to “the security situation in the north of the Cabo Delgado” ; “Total expresses its solidarity with the government and people of Mozambique and wishes that the actions carried out by the government of Mozambique and its regional and international partners will enable the restoration of security and stability in Cabo Delgado province in a sustained manner.”

a7347.speaker: National Petroleum Institute (INP) (statement)
a7347.name: National Petroleum Institute (INP) (statement)
a7347.speech: warned that Total’s action could lead to Total “suspending or cancelling more contracts with suppliers of goods and services.”

a7347.speaker: Joao Osvaldo Moisees Macatine, Public Works Minister
a7347.name: Joao Osvaldo Moisees Macatine
a7347.title: Public Works Minister
a7347.speech: said ENI’s floating LNG platform should arrive in early 2022; the platform costs $8 bn, and should generate profits of $41 mn per year, of which $19 mn eventually goes to government.

a7347.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, President of Mozambique
a7347.name: Filipe Nyusi
a7347.title: President of Mozambique
a7347.speech: on 21 April promised to ensure that the distribution of wealth from natural resources is structured, fair, inclusive and sustainable, to benefit every citizen in the country ; addressing the opening session in Maputo of the 7th Conference and Exhibition on Mining, Oil, Gas and Energy, Nyusi said Mozambique wants to avoid the experiences of other countries, which failed to use the wealth from their resources to develop their own economies.

a7347.speaker: Credit Suisse
a7347.name: Credit Suisse
a7347.speech: announced Brian Chin, chief executive of the investment bank, and Lara Warner, chief risk and compliance officer, would leave the bank.

a7347.speaker: Wall Street Journal (8 April)
a7347.name: Wall Street Journal (8 April)
a7347.speech: noted that CS is “a bank that looked the other way when warning signs argued for pulling back on lucrative corners of its business,” and that in the case of Greensill there had been “years of internal warnings.”

a7347.speaker: Credit Suisse (January 2020 investor presentation)
a7347.name: Credit Suisse (January 2020 investor presentation)
a7347.speech: a presentation that said Greensill was a “once in a generation” investment chance that “any growth investor must own”.

a7347.speaker: Rishi Sunak, UK Chancellor (finance minister)
a7347.name: Rishi Sunak
a7347.title: UK Chancellor (finance minister)
a7347.speech: On 23 Apr Sunak texted Cameron to say Greensill would be helped.

a7347.speaker: Boris Johnson, UK Prime Minister
a7347.name: Boris Johnson
a7347.title: UK Prime Minister
a7347.speech: a text exchange with Tory donor and vacuum cleaner maker James Dyson in which Johnson agrees to sort out a tax problem “tomorrow”.

a7347.speaker: The Guardian (23, 24 April)
a7347.name: The Guardian (23
a7347.title: 24 April)
a7347.speech: reported that the UK has government by text and WhatsApp, that many people have Prime Minister Boris Johnson’s phone number, which has not been changed in a decade, and that there was a text message from Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and a text exchange with James Dyson.

a7394.speaker: Residents of Altadena, devastated Los Angeles suburb
a7394.name: Residents of Altadena
a7394.title: devastated Los Angeles suburb
a7394.speech: Said the arrival of men of the National Guard soldiers was too little and late, the AFP reports.

a7394.speaker: Nicholas Norman, 40, teacher, Altadena resident
a7394.name: Nicholas Norman
a7394.title: 40, teacher, Altadena resident
a7394.speech: “We didn't see a single firefighter while we were throwing buckets of water to defend our house against the flames” ; “They were too busy over in the Palisades saving the rich and famous's properties, and they let us common folks burn.”

a7394.speaker: Nicole Perri, 32, stylist, Pacific Palisades resident
a7394.name: Nicole Perri
a7394.title: 32, stylist, Pacific Palisades resident
a7394.speech: “Our city has completely let us down,” outraged by the fact that hydrants being used by firefighters ran dry or lost pressure; in a state of shock, she wants to see accountability: “Things should have been in place that could have prevented this” ; “We've lost everything, and I just feel zero support from our city, our horrible mayor and our governor.”

a7394.speaker: James Brown, 65-year-old retired lawyer in Altadena
a7394.name: James Brown
a7394.title: 65-year-old retired lawyer in Altadena
a7394.speech: “I don't think the officials were prepared at all” ; “There's going to have to be a real evaluation here, because hundreds and hundreds of thousands of people have just been completely displaced.”
